  • Sources indicate that artificial-intelligence agents have already begun to wreak havoc by hacking into servers around the world, either spontaneously or directed by humans.
  • Several computer scientists have suggested on social media that the leading AI laboratories — companies such as OpenAI and Anthropic, both in San Francisco, California — have discovered algorithms that could derail the security of Internet communications.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Public-key cryptography helps to secure everything from online banking and private messages to sensitive government communications.Credit: Peshkov/Getty.

Sources indicate that artificial-intelligence agents have already begun to wreak havoc by hacking into servers around the world, either spontaneously or directed by humans. Now, a threat is emerging that is on a whole other scale.

Several computer scientists have suggested on social media that the leading AI laboratories — companies such as OpenAI and Anthropic, both in San Francisco, California — have discovered algorithms that could derail the security of Internet communications.

‘If we can solve Riemann, what can’t we do?’: mathematicians shocked and excited by AI breakthroughs.

‘If we can solve Riemann, what can’t we do?’: mathematicians shocked and excited by AI breakthroughs.

“I’m virtually certain, from multiple reliable sources, that the AI labs are now sitting on one or more bombshells,” computer scientist Scott Aaronson wrote yesterday on his blog. The details are still hazy, added Aaronson, who is at the University of Texas at Austin. “Until I either see details or hear directly from someone at a lab, I feel much, much less confident about the specific nature of those bombshells.”.

The algorithms are rumoured to target the information-scrambling system known as RSA, which relies on the mathematics of prime numbers, as well as more-advanced technologies.

While the rumours could not be confirmed, other breakthroughs announced by the AI companies this week make researchers cautiously optimistic that the mathematics of encryption could eventually come to help.

Nature examines the threat, and what can be done about it.

Several researchers say they have heard that some of the leading AI laboratories have discovered algorithms capable of breaking public-key cryptography in ‘polynomial time’ (or ‘P’ in computer-science shorthand).

Public-key cryptography helps to secure everything from banking apps to Internet browsers. It relies on mathematical problems that are considered practically impossible for computers to solve within a reasonable amount of time.

An algorithm that could solve these problems in polynomial time would change that. It means the time needed to solve a problem would increase relatively slowly as the problem gets larger. For example, a password of length n could be broken in a number of steps proportional to the square or cube of its size (n² or n³).

The race to save the Internet from quantum hackers.

The race to save the Internet from quantum hackers.

Theoretical computer scientists tend to think of P problems as relatively easy to solve, especially compared with problems that require exponential time, where the number of steps might grow as 2n, for example. As n gets larger — or a password gets longer — the time required by an exponential algorithm promptly exceeds that of any polynomial one.

In practical terms, an algorithm that could break public-key cryptography in polynomial time could undermine much of the security on which the Internet relies.

It depends on which encryption systems they could crack, and how efficiently they could do so.

According to recent reports, one of the most ubiquitous techniques for establishing public keys is to multiply two large prime numbers. This technique, called RSA, was long believed to be secure because ‘cracking the code’ requires factoring that product back into the original primes, a much slower process (at least, without a powerful quantum computer, which does not yet exist). One of the rumours now circulating is that the AI labs have found an algorithm that can do this.

But even though a polynomial-time algorithm could be very powerful on paper, it could still be impossible to use except for the shortest passwords. An algorithm requiring n10000steps, for example, be very impractical to apply.

However, proving that a problem is in ‘P’, even if the polynomial-time solution is practically useless, has usually been followed by improvements that have eventually led to efficient solutions. “The concern is that the idea that [the problem] was hard — because of needing exponential time — is dead,” Aaronson tells Nature.

Not necessarily. This type of worst-case scenario hinges on a long-standing open question known as ‘P = NP’: could every problem whose solution can be checked in polynomial time also be solved in polynomial time? If so, problems that underpin essentially all public-key cryptography could become much easier to crack.

Quantum-computing pioneer warns of complacency over Internet security.

Quantum-computing pioneer warns of complacency over Internet security.

Recent findings suggest that but most researchers think that this is unlikely. In fact, some recent AI-aided results have made them cautiously optimistic. Earlier this week, both Anthropic and OpenAI revealed results in theoretical computer science that suggest that many similar problems could be hard to solve. Before the recent explosion in AI-aided maths, each of those advances would have been hailed as the computer-science breakthrough of the decade, Aaronson indicates.

Ryan Williams, a computer scientist at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology in Cambridge, agrees. “I am definitely blown away by the latest developments.” One especially interesting result, he states, indicates that for a ubiquitous type of computation called matrix multiplication, the exponent in a polynomial-time algorithm cannot be too small. “Underneath the hood, it seems to provide a brand-new framework for proving limitations on efficient computation,” says Williams.

doi: https://doi.org/10.1038/d41586-026-03875-6.

Latest Update: Bella Hadid Shares Multiple Health Diagnoses That "Deeply” Impact Her

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Bella Hadid is sharing fresh revelations about her health.
  • The 30-year-old explained how managing several medical conditions in addition to Lyme disease—which her mom, Yolanda Hadid, first shared her daughter had in 2015—impacts her, explaining, "My body just can’t connect with my brain.".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Bella Hadid is sharing fresh revelations about her health.

The 30-year-old explained how managing several medical conditions in addition to Lyme disease—which her mom, Yolanda Hadid, first shared her daughter had in 2015—impacts her, explaining, "My body just can’t connect with my brain.".

"I have POTS, and I have a lot of PMDD, endometriosis," Bella told Harper's Bazaar in an interview published Nov. 23. "Plus my Lyme and things that affect my body very deeply.".

While premenstrual dysphoric disorder and endometriosis are illnesses related to the female reproductive system that cause painful and exhausting menstrual cycles, according to the Cleveland Clinic, postural orthostatic tachycardia is a syndrome that causes a person's heart to beat faster when they change the position of their body.

And in speaking about her diagnoses, the Beauty actress was brought back to a time when a frightening flare-up threatened to keep her off the runway.

"Right before I walked out on the runway for my opening look, I went to go stretch and my whole clavicle completely—," she recounted. "I don’t even know what it was. My lungs almost collapsed, and I couldn’t breathe.".

And with her following the family business in fashion along with Yolanda's other two kids, Gigi Hadid, 31, and Anwar Hadid, 27, Bella admitted the painful interruptions shake her confidence to perform.

"My body goes through these different motions of feeling really good and then all of a sudden crashing on me at the worst moments," she continued. "Because I know how to walk. One thing I can do is I can strut. But it’s a lot of pressure; we all have our own insecurities.".

With that in mind, the Victoria's Secret Angel has to remind herself, "maybe my body can’t handle all that I have going on," which ultimately results in the freedom to decide, "'No, we can’t do that today.'".

Earlier this year, the model—who recently went public with her relationship with boyfriend Nathan Lacy—explained how her health struggles can feel isolating.

"Sometimes it feels like unless you've lived something like this, or loved someone who has," Bella captioned a June 26 Instagram Story, "it's impossible to understand.".

Read on for more stars who have walked the world through their health challenges.

Travis Barker's Precancer Diagnosis.

The Blink-182 drummer stopped smoking weed after being diagnosed with "precancer of the esophagus.".

Industry observers note that "I loved blunts and I would smoke too much," he shared on a November 2026 episode of the Significant Bro with Kid Cudi podcast, recalling how his doctor mentioned it was a "serious case. "He’s like, ‘This is your warning shot. Don’t f--l around. You’ve got to stop smoking.".

The Jessie alum opened up about her "hellish" migraines, sharing how they've worsened after suffering five concussions over the course of her life.

According to recent reports, "The brain injuries make things significantly worse," Ryan shared during a September 2026 episode of Mythical Kitchen’s Last Meals. "I had a pretty crazy, life-altering brain injury a few years ago, and I was out of commission for six months.".

While Ryan described her first four concussions as "incidents," she said her fifth one was trauma caused by "sustained shaking over a minute of time.".

Now, the former Disney Channel star needs to close her eyes to "think better.".

"Quite often the world is really loud. It’s really too bright. There’s a lot going on," she explained. "The visual data that I'm taking in can be so distracting and so loud. Then, with the migraines—which are significantly worsened by that—it sort of is too much.".

Brianna "Chickenfry" LaPaglia's Ovarian Cyst.

In May 2026, the BFFs podcaster underwent emergency surgery after doctors discovered a large ovarian cyst that had been twisting her organs and causing internal bleeding.

"There was a half a liter of blood in my pelvic floor," Brianna shared in a TikTok video after the operation. "I have five incisions all over my stomach. They went in through my belly button with a camera so they could find all the blood.".

Nikki Garcia's Breast Implant Injury.

The Total Bellas alum revealed that one of her breast implants shifted after an elbow slam from fellow WWE star Piper Niven during a July 2025 wrestling match.

In a recent development, "It's OK," she told sister Bella Garcia at the time. "We're going to get it fixed one day. I told the doctor, I go, 'Newly divorced, so the minute the boots are hung up, I'm going to come back to you and we're going to make these girls look real good, because these girls are going to get some action in the future and that can't look like that.'".

In October 2026, the former The Bachelorette star detailed how she cracked a vertebra in her spine after setting her vibration plate—a motorized platform that rapidly moves back and forth to promote muscle activation and circulation—to "level 30, supersonic speed.".

"Seemingly, subtly, somewhere on the way to 30, maybe 10 or 20, my vertebrae turn crooked and rub against each other," Windey shared in a Substack essaye aptly titled "Broke back, no mountain.".

"It was too fast vibrations I guess, and too many vibrations maybe, and too much pressure to shake," she continued. "And it broke. Broke right off, like your ex-boyfriend’s bumper. Well, technically, it cracked.".

The injury left her with what she described as "insatiable" paresthesia—a medical term for a tingling, pins-and-needles sensation.

In a recent development, "This is the greatest sense of condemnation; of persecution, I’ll ever feel," she added. "And I do wish it on my worst enemy If only they hadn’t wished it on me first.".

Lupita Nyong'o's Uterine Fibroids.

The 12 Years a Slave star was diagnosed with uterine fibroids—non-cancerous growths that develop in or around the uterus—in 2014, the same year she won an Oscar for performance in the movie.

However, it wasn't until 2025 when she disclosed her diagnosis, writing on Instagram that she had been "suffering in silence" for more than a decade.

"When we reach puberty, we're taught periods mean pain, and that pain is simply part of being a woman," she shared. "We're struggling alone with something that affects us most.".

Brian Austin Green's Perforated Appendix.

The Beverly Hills, 90210 alum revealed in April 2025 that he was recovering from surgery after his appendix nearly burst.

In a recent development, “Last week, I started feeling some pain in my stomach,” Brian stated in an Instagram video at the time. “I ended up going to the emergency room, and I had a perforated appendix. Not quite burst, but just before.”.

In a recent development, he added, “I'm on the road to recovery. It's not an easy process. This is my first major surgery.”.

In July 2025, the Daisy Jones & The Six star shared that she had been hospitalized due to a hernia—a gap in the muscular wall that's commonly found in the abdomen or groin area—caused by wearing tight pants.

Recent findings suggest that "'Suki you never tweet anymore,'" she wrote on X, formerly known as Twitter. "Have you ever considered I wore pants so tight 6 months ago it caused a hernia & I’ve been too scared to tell you?".

Savannah DeMelo's Mid-Game "Medical Emergency" Mid-Game.

The Racing Louisville midfielder collapsed just a few minutes into her soccer team's September 2025 match against Seattle Reign at Lumen Field in Seatle.

It has been revealed that the United States Women’s National Team player could be seen slowly sitting down on the field with a teammate by her side, per Reuters, as the referee called for trainers to check her out. She collapsed seconds later.

Sources indicate that “Savannah received immediate on-field care from medical personnel and was transported to a local hospital for further evaluation,” the National Women’s Soccer League wrote on X later that night. “She is stable and alert.".

Adam Devine's Long-Term Injury From Childhood Accident.

Adam Devine shared that injuries he sustained after getting hit by a cement truck when he was 11 years old are still affecting him to this day.

“It’s been a nightmare,” Devine said in a 2025 episode of the In Depth With Graham Bensinger podcast. “I have spasms all over. For a while, [the doctors] told me I was dying—literally, within this last year.”.

He noted that pain comes and goes, adding, "My body has all these things that are a little wonky and a little wrong with it.".

The Bachelor Nation alum shared that he went to the hospital “crawling on all fours” due to overwhelming back pain that was aggravated during an RV trip with a friend.

“Right now, knees to my toes, it’s, like, still tingly, which is crazy,” he said on a March 2025 episode of his Trading Secrets podcast. “And to put in perspective, I don’t know, man, like not to sound douchey, but like two, three weeks ago, maybe a month ago, I was squatting probably like 295 pounds. And right now, I can’t do a squat on my foot. I can’t do a one legged squat, I fall. It’s like I had a stroke or something.”.

But with the help of a back specialist and some steroids, he added, “We’re on the mend.”.

Matt Kirschenheiter's Heart Attack.

Real Housewives of Orange County’s Gina Kirschenheiter shared her ex-husband Matt Kirschenheiter suffered a heart attack in March 2025, but thankfully survived the ordeal.

Tracy Morgan's Medical Emergency.

The 30 Rock star suffered a health scare at a Upcoming York Knicks basketball game in March 2025, leading to him being wheeled out of Madison Square Garden.

However, the comedian shared an update on social media the following day, noting it was a case of food poisoning and that he was on the mend.

Christy Carlson Romano's Eye Injury.

The Even Stevens alum shared in February 2025 that she was shot in the face while on a trip to shoot clay pigeons to celebrate husband Brendan Rooney's birthday.

Industry observers note that "There was another party with us and they unsafely fired in the wrong direction and shot me in the face," she wrote on Instagram. "@thebrendanrooney immediately sprung into action, assessed me, and rushed me to the hospital. I was hit in 5 places, one was less than an inch from hitting me directly in my right eye.".

The Kim Possible alum continued, "Unfortunately a fragment got lodged behind my eye and it is too risky to remove surgically at this time. Doctors will continue to monitor me (I can see normally at the moment).".

The actress stated she was grateful to be alive. "I love my daughters, husband, family, and friends so much," she said. "I saw my life flash before my eyes and I’m telling you, hug the people around you every chance you can. Life can change in an instant.".

Industry observers note that while the internet isn't always a kind place, Amy Schumer is happy that, in this case, it helped her get answers."The internet really came for me after doing a bunch of press, and I was like, 'OK everybody, relax,'" Amy recalled of her "puffier" face on a January 2025 episode of Call Her Daddy. "But then doctors were chiming in in the comments and they were like, 'No no, we think something’s really up. Your face looks so crazy that we think something’s up. And I’m like, ‘Wait, I’m getting trolled by doctors?’"After these doctors said they thought she had Cushing syndrome and that it may be caused by spiking coritsol levels or steroid injections, the Life & Beth creator thought, "Wait, I have been getting steroid injections in my scars.""I had a breast reduction, a C-section, whatever, and so I was getting these steroid injections," Amy said. "So it gave me this thing called Cushing syndrome, which I wouldn’t have known if the internet hadn’t come for me so hard."Toda, Amy is just relieved she's OK. As she shared in a February 2024 News Not Noise newsletter, "Finding out I have the kind of Cushing that will just work itself out and I'm healthy was the greatest news imaginable.".

Casey Fitzgerald's Neck Injury From Hockey Skate Blade.

The AHL player was cut by a fellow player's skate during a game in December 2024 and received 25 stitches. His father, New Jersey Devils general manager Tom Fitzgerald later told ESPN after his son was fully recovered, "We're very lucky. I don't wish that on any parent.".

Hailey Bieber had the "scariest moment" of her life when she was having breakfast with husband Justin Bieber and started experiencing stroke-like symptoms in March 2022."Justin was like, 'Are you OK?'" the Rhode skincare mogul shared a month later on YouTube, "and I just didn't respond because I wasn't sure. And then he asked me again and when I went to respond, I couldn't speak. The right side of my face started drooping. I couldn't get a sentence out."While Hailey remarked the facial drooping stopped and her speech came back, she went to the hospital to make sure she was OK."They did some scans and they were able to see that I had suffered a small blood clot to my brain," the model added, "which they labeled and categorized as something called a TIA [Transient Ischemic Attack]."Later, Hailey went to the University of California, Los Angeles, where she found out she had a hole in her heart called a patent foramen ovale (PFO).She explained the blood clot had traveled into her heart, "escaped" through the hole and went to her brain, leading to the TIA.Hailey said she had a successful PFO closure procedure and was now feeling great.

Justin Bieber's Ramsay Hunt Syndrome.

The same year Hailey had her health scare, Justin experienced one of his own.In June 2022, the "Baby" singer shared he was diagnosed with Ramsay Hunt syndrome, a condition that caused temporary paralysis to parts of his face and forced him to cancel the remainder of his Justice World Tour."It is from this virus that attacks the nerve in my ear and my facial nerves and has caused my face to have paralysis," Justin explained in an Instagram video at the time. "As you can see, this eye is not blinking. I can't smile on this side of my face. This nostril will not move. So, there's full paralysis on this side of my face."In fact, he told his followers it had gotten "progressively harder to eat." But after a while, the paralysis went away."He's doing really well," Hailey said on a June 2022 episode of Good Morning America, later adding, "He's feeling a lot better. Obviously, it was just a very scary and random situation to happen, but he's going to be totally OK and I'm just grateful that he's fine.".

Jamie Foxx's Brain Bleed & Stroke.

Industry observers note that while Jamie Foxx initially kept details of his April 2023 hospitalization private, he later opened up about what he went through.One day in Atlanta, "I was having such a bad headache, so I asked my boy, I mentioned, ‘Listen, I need an aspirin,’” the Oscar winner said in his 2024 Netflix special What Had Happened Was... “Before I could get the Aspirin, I went out. I don’t remember 20 days.”Jamie said he was initially taken to a doctor who gave him a cortisone shot and then sent him home. However, his concerned sister Deidra Dixon then drove him to a hospital, where they got an answer: He had a brain bleed that led to a stroke.Twenty days after undergoing an operation, the Django Unchained woke up May 4 in a wheelchair and couldn’t walk. He then went to Chicago for rehabilitation and therapy."All I can tell you is that I appreciate every prayer,” he said, “because I needed every prayer.”.

Tracey Yukich's Medical Emergency on The Biggest Loser.

The reality star revealed that she "died" while running a mile during the first challenge of the NBC competition series.

In a recent development, “I don't remember a lot,” she explained on Fit for TV: The Reality of The Biggest Loser. “I remember hearing the helicopter. I just felt like I was floating. And then my grandpa was there. And then I saw darkness. But then I saw light. So I knew, I knew I died that day.”.

Industry observers note that “My organs were literally shutting down,” she continued. “I didn't realize that I had rhabdomyolysis. And rhabdomyolysis is your body's way of saying, ‘I'm going to shut down on you.’”.

Emilia Clarke filmed battle scenes for Game of Thrones, but in 2019, she published an essay in The Upcoming Yorker titled "A Battle for My Life."Having a bad headache at the gym, "I reached the toilet, sank to my knees, and proceeded to be violently, voluminously ill," the actress wrote. "Meanwhile, the pain—shooting, stabbing, constricting pain—was getting worse. At some level, I knew what was happening: my brain was damaged."She was taken to the hospital for a brain scan."The diagnosis was quick and ominous: a subarachnoid hemorrhage (SAH), a life-threatening type of stroke, caused by bleeding into the space surrounding the brain," the Emmy nominee added. "I’d had an aneurysm, an arterial rupture."Emilia had immediate surgery to seal the aneurysm, calling the pain "unbearable." While she was recovering, she continued, she experienced aphasia and was "muttering nonsense."A week later, "the aphasia passed," Emilia added, and she left the hospital a month after being admitted. At a 2013 brain scan, she learned a growth "doubled in size" and that she needed surgery again."When they woke me, I was screaming in pain," she wrote. "The procedure had failed. I had a massive bleed and the doctors made it plain that my chances of surviving were precarious if they didn’t operate again. This time they needed to access my brain in the old-fashioned way—through my skull."Thankfully, Emilia shared, she's now "at a hundred per cent.".

Snoop Dogg's daughter Cori Broadus is grateful for her family.Because after she suffered a "severe stroke" in January 2024, her loved ones rushed to be by her side."I texted them that I just had a stroke and sent them a picture," she told E! News correspondent Will Marfuggi in December 2024. "Everybody just came to my rescue."Because of other medical concerns, Cori ended up staying in the hospital longer than she initially expected."I could have went home after my stroke, but my lupus wasn't doing so well," the Snoop's Fatherhood: Cori and Wayne's Story star continued. "My kidneys were failing. It was a lot going on."Today, Cori is on the mend."I'm doing great," she added. "I just had a little bit of motor skills that I had to work back on. But other than that, I was fine.".

Shailene Woodley's Health Battle.

Shailene Woodley’s early 20s were not an easy time health-wise.“It got to the point where I was losing my hearing. I couldn’t walk for longer than five minutes at a time without having to lay down for hours, and hours and sleep. Everything I ate hurt my stomach,” the actress remarked on a September 2024 episode of the SHE MD Podcast. “It was this conflation of issues and diagnoses and different doctors telling me different things.”So Shailene—who chose to keep the exact condition private—set out to find answers. “I come from a very holistic background and study herbalism,” she added. “So I was very keen on, ‘I’m going to work with real MDs, [and] I’m also going to work with independent kind of healers.’ Just trying to search for some sense of comfort in my own skin.”It was a long journey—one that lasted for 10 years.“Throughout that decade, a lot of other things came from feeling so much discomfort physically,” the Massive Little Lies star noted, “which was, ‘My gosh, if everything I eat hurts my stomach, I’m now suddenly afraid of food.’ And then going into the kind of mental f--ckery that can happen with that of body dysmorphia and confusion about identity and feeling safe in my own capsule, in my own skin, what that meant, and what that should be.”After tending to both her physical and mental health, Shailene is feeling much better.“It was a journey that ultimately physically resolved itself, and I am very healthy,” she shared. “I’m so happy to be able to say that.".

Calvert-Lewin joined Leeds United in 2025 after nine years at Everton.

Dominic Calvert-Lewin has signed a new contract to stay with Leeds United until 2029.

The former Everton striker, 29, has five goals and one assist so far in the Premier League this season, with Daniel Farke's side sitting seventh in the table.

Confirmation of Calvert-Lewin's deal follows speculation about his future at the club, with reports that he was interesting Manchester United.

Calvert-Lewin scored 15 goals across all competitions during his first season at Elland Road after joining in August 2025, and the form earned him an England recall in March.

He was also called up by Thomas Tuchel this autumn and came off the bench in England's wins against Czech Republic and Spain.

He scored a penalty and had an assist in Leeds' 4-1 thrashing of Chelsea on Saturday.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Just call her the Real Housewife of Maple Brook, Texas.

Hunting Wives star Jaime Ray Newman revealed that when it comes to her character Callie Baskin, she was inspired by The Real Housewives of Dallas' fan favorite Momma Dee Simmons, mother of Housewife D'Andra Simmons.

It has been revealed that "When I was auditioning for Callie, I became obsessed with Real Housewives of Dallas," Newman exclusively told E! News at the season two premiere. "I had Momma Dee in my ears for about a week, just listening to her over and over and over again.".

According to recent reports, even though Newman confessed that she wasn't previously "a reality TV person," the matriarch's larger-than-life personality helped her tap into a Texas socialite's persona. That’s especially true for Hunting Wives season two—hitting Netflix Nov. 26—because Callie and the other wives of Maple Brook become stars of their own over-the-top reality TV show, Married Justice.

As the 48-year-old explained, "When I read the first scripts, I'm like, 'Oh my god, I gotta go into full reality TV show mode.'".

As such, her creative process included "thinking, 'What would Callie pick and choose?' Like, little things, little ways to pose, little 'isms' that Callie would lean into," adding that it was fascinating to deep dive "into something I didn't know that much about.".

And returning to set with costars Brittany Snow and Malin Akerman after season one only encouraged Newman to make her performance even more dramatic.

According to recent reports, "Seeing the show fully realized, now we got to really let loose," the Eastwick alum remarked. "I feel like season two was just much more wild.".

It has been revealed that that said, Newman's work is already resonating with fans, including the Real Housewives of Potomac's Karen Huger. While the Bravo star said reuniting with her real-life friend group this year has been "wonderful," she also volunteered herself for any future openings on the Hunting Wives cast, quipping, "all things are possible.".

For now, the series has added the WNBA star Angel Reese for its second season. As for what the 24-year-old—who has acted in GOAT and A House of Dynamite—mentioned viewers will take away from her role?

"Barbie," Reese mused, referencing her character's name, Trainer Barbie. "I'm just the Barbie, being myself.".

Industry News: On this day in space! Nov. 24, 1947: The US Navy launches the 1st Aerobee sounding rocket, but it didn't reach space

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (629 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Space

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Navy debuted the first Aerobee rocket into the sky, but it never reached space.
  • Aerobee was a suborbital sounding rocket designed to study Earth's atmosphere.
  • After World War 2, the United States started reusing erman V-2 rockets for this kind of research.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, on Nov. 24, 1947, the U.S. Navy debuted the first Aerobee rocket into the sky, but it never reached space.

Aerobee was a suborbital sounding rocket designed to study Earth's atmosphere.

After World War 2, the United States started reusing erman V-2 rockets for this kind of research. When they started running out of V-2 rockets, the United States constructed its own rockets that were similar but cheaper to build and to launch. In the weeks leading up to the first Aerobee mission, three test flights were released.

Industry observers note that those tests used a dummy version of Aerobee with a live booster to see if the two stages would separate properly. On Aerobee's first real flight, the rocket flew about 35 miles high. That's below the 62-mile (100 kilometers) upper limit for the boundary of space. (NASA and the U.S. military typically consider 50 miles the edge of space.) Mission control cut the flight short after about 30 seconds, because Aerobee started to yaw, and they wanted to keep it from going completely out of control.

Billed as the "most successful sounding rocket of the space age," the initial Aerobee rocket was suborbital rocket designed to launch experment payload of up to 100 pounds (45 kilograms) to an altitude of 75 miles (121 kilometers) or so.

"The Aerobee was designed to carry instruments aloft to collect data on the upper atmosphere and to place small animals in a weightless condition for physiological studies," the U.S. National Museum of the United States Air Force wrote in a mission overview. "It was rolled out by a solid-propellant booster engine of 18,000 pounds thrust that burned for only two and a half seconds.".

While the first Aerobee rocket did not reach space, many more made successful rolls out in the decades that followed.

Engineers made a steady stream of upgrades to the the Aerobee rocket, allowing to fly higher and launch heavier payloads into space. It was an Aerobee rocket that debuted two Phillipine monkeys on a mission to study how the effects of rapid launch acceleration might affect their bodies, an experiment that was among the frst human physiology tests that paved the way for human spaceflight.

More than 1,000 Aerobee rockets have released since then, and the last one flew in January of 1985.

As an editor with over 10 years of experience in science journalism she has previously written for Scholastic Classroom Magazines, MedPage Today and The Joint Institute for Computational Sciences at Oak Ridge National Laboratory. After studying physics at the University of Tennessee in her hometown of Knoxville, she earned her graduate degree in Science, Health and Environmental Reporting (SHERP) from Upcoming York University. Hanneke joined the Space.com team in 2016 as a staff writer and producer, covering topics including spaceflight and astronomy. She presently lives in Seattle, home of the Space Needle, with her cat and two snakes. In her spare time, Hanneke enjoys exploring the Rocky Mountains, basking in nature and looking for dark skies to gaze at the cosmos.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Alejandro Garnacho's time at Aston Villa has been brief - and it already looks to be over.
  • The latest snub by Villa boss Unai Emery was the most damming of all, with the on-loan Chelsea winger left out of Tuesday's Champions League defeat at Galatasaray.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Alejandro Garnacho is yet to start a game for Aston Villa this season.

Alejandro Garnacho's time at Aston Villa has been brief - and it already looks to be over.

The latest snub by Villa boss Unai Emery was the most damming of all, with the on-loan Chelsea winger left out of Tuesday's Champions League defeat at Galatasaray.

"The players who were here I think are the best players to be here with us," said Emery.

Villa could have had 12 substitutes in Istanbul but Emery chose just 11 - including two goalkeepers - as Garnacho stayed at home.

The plan was for the Argentina international's loan move to become permanent for Â£43m should certain criteria be met.

They are believed to be based on a number of appearances staff felt were so achievable the club were in little doubt he would become a Villa player.

But now there is doubt he will ever play for them again.

Garnacho trained with Villa's first team on Monday but did not travel to Istanbul.

According to recent reports, "First start after three months. Happy to be enjoying football again.".

The post Garnacho wrote on social media after a pre-season game in July has - along with anything else related to Villa - been deleted from his account.

He has played just 34 minutes in the Premier League this season, and seven of Villa's 11 games ended without him getting on the pitch.

His last appearance - just a three-minute cameo - came in the 1-1 draw against Fulham on 31 October.

Including Saturday's 0-0 draw with Sunderland, Garnacho has been omitted from the past three matchday squads - a strong sign Emery has lost faith in him.

But he may have been fighting a losing battle from the off, having arrived at Villa unfit.

Sources have acknowledged the 22-year-old was not at the level required and were surprised how off the pace he was when he signed in July.

He initially trained on his own, and questions over the signing were already being asked, with eyebrows raised by some internally given his inconsistent form for both Chelsea and Manchester United.

Yet he had been on Villa's list of targets - albeit a long list - while he was at Stamford Bridge as Emery was keen to sign a pacy winger in the summer.

Garnacho's problems were compounded by a head injury suffered in Thailand in pre-season, and even a boot camp during the international break in September and October, and scoring in friendlies against Sevilla and Southampton have not helped.

One of the issues Villa have is there is no exit clause, and both teams would have to agree to end the season-long loan deal early.

This time last year, Emery had already decided not to sign Harvey Elliott permanently in a Â£30m deal, leaving the on-loan Liverpool midfielder in limbo for the rest of the season.

And it appears Emery has already come to the same conclusion with Garnacho.

Sources indicate that with Villa unable to find a solution with Liverpool, Elliott wasted a precious year of his career. Those close to him recognise the damage last season did, playing just nine times after being named Player of the Tournament at the European Under-21 Championship in 2025.

He is now at Valencia and is yet to start in La Liga this season.

Recent findings suggest that the risk of going on loan to Villa became a topic of conversation in the game because of Elliott's plight, with sources suggesting players would think twice about joining the club. Garnacho's situation only increases those concerns.

Three times in two seasons, Emery and Villa have signed a high-profile player on loan only for it to fail.

Jadon Sancho's expensive loan from Manchester United last season - Villa paying a guaranteed 80% of Sancho's wages of more than Â£200,000 a week - ended with him having made just nine Premier League starts and scoring once in 39 appearances, with 21 of those as a substitute.

Sancho may have played more than Elliott and Garnacho - and came off the bench in their Europa League final win - but what value did Villa really get?

Of course, Marcus Rashford and Marco Asensio enjoyed positive loan spells previously - Rashford returning to the England squad while at Villa - but they are exceptions to the rule.

Nicolo Zaniolo, Clement Lenglet and Axel Disasi have joined in recent years and barely merit footnotes, while Douglas Luiz's loan return last season did not prompt a return to the heights he had reached previously at Villa.

The club have constantly complained about financial restrictions with some justification, but questions can certainly be asked about the money spent on many of their signings.

The blunt truth is there is no clear path.

Teenager George Hemmings has just signed a new deal and has earned praise from Emery for understanding the way he wants his players to work.

Ibrahim Mbaye and Alysson are also ahead of Garnacho, leaving him well behind even before regulars John McGinn, Johan Manzambi and Emi Buendia are factored in.

There was interest from abroad in the summer, with Roma keen, and it seems increasingly unlikely we will see Garnacho at another Premier League club soon.

Fifa rules allow players to play for two clubs in a season - or three if they move to a team whose season overlaps like the MLS - meaning Garnacho could feature for another, unlike Elliott as he had already played for Liverpool and Villa.

Sources indicate that garnacho, whose character has not been called into question while at Villa, cost Chelsea Â£40m when he signed from Manchester United in 2025 but failed to make a consistent impression, with eight goals in 43 games. When he joined Chelsea he signed a contract until 2032.

Prior to that, United boss Ruben Amorim had told him to leave.

Now nothing, it seems, will persuade Emery that Garnacho is worth persevering with - leaving the winger's career continuing to drift.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • In a recent development, the best robot vacuums these days aren’t just vacuuming your floors, nor are they blindly bumping around your house like they used to.
  • In a recent development, here are the best robot vacuum cleaners I’ve tried this year, and everything we really liked from recent years.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

I've recently introduced a few friends to the power of a great robot vacuum. One of my friends calls hers a marriage saver, while the other was both thrilled and horrified by how many stains the vacuum’s AI found on her floors. Personally, my robot vacuums keep me from wanting to set the litter box on fire, since my cat is on a mission to create his own navigational trail of litter through my home.

In a recent development, the best robot vacuums these days aren’t just vacuuming your floors, nor are they blindly bumping around your house like they used to. These gadgets are mopping, scrubbing away stains, lifting themselves off obstacles, and even reminding you to clean the dirtier areas in your home more frequently. A good robot vacuum can cost a pretty penny, but it doesn’t have to, depending on what you’re looking for. Which is the best model for you? I’ve been testing every upcoming robot vacuum I can in my three-story home filled with three adults, a preschooler, and a cat.

In a recent development, here are the best robot vacuum cleaners I’ve tried this year, and everything we really liked from recent years. Looking for more vacuum ideas? Don't miss our guides to the Best Dyson Vacuums, Best Cordless Vacuums, Best Vacuums for Pet Hair, Best Carpet Cleaners, and Best Vacuums.

Recent findings suggest that updated November 2026: The Roborock Qrevo 2 Pro is now this guide's budget pick, with the Eufy Omni C28 as a budget runner-up. I've also added the Roborock Saros 20 Flow to Honorable Mentions, and testing notes on the Dyson Nurovi R3, Tapo RV50 Pro Omni, and three iRobot Roomba models (Max 875, Plus 678, and Plus 575). I've also ensured up-to-date links and prices.

I’ve been testing the latest models from our favorite cleaning brands. Here are the top three I’d buy right now.

I was surprised how much I liked the AI-powered Shark PowerDetect UV Reveal. Its UV light revealed spots on my floor where I know I previously had spills, and its built-in AI had the vacuum go back over to deep-clean those spots in a way I clearly hadn’t done before. The UV Reveal also did a great job on my hard floors (both LVP and tile) as a mop-and-vacuum combo, as well as on my builder-grade carpet and a large rug in the living room. I was impressed that the rug actually felt just as fluffy and well-vacuumed as if I had cracked out my favorite Dyson stick vacuum instead of just sending a robot vacuum to do the work for me.

It has an extendable arm, which did a good job passing my corner test. I stuck three Cheerios in tricky corners of my home, and it got two out of three, doing better than the latest Dyson vacuum. It managed to get the trickier two corners too; it skipped the third Cheerio to avoid bumping my bar stools. I also did a spill test with two spots of cherry juice in my home. It mopped away the first spill with no problem, but I did have to send it back out to finish cleaning the second spill. The UV Reveal did great with obstacle avoidance and has “NeverStuck Technology” to lift itself off obstacles, and it worked to get itself off the flat, long legs of one of my side tables. The vacuum finished a cleaning run in a good amount of time, cleaning my entire main floor in about 60 minutes, but it does go back out to scrub all the spots it sees on the floor. That took another 30 minutes for me, but I assume that would get shorter over time, the longer you live with this vacuum and have it cleaning up. Still, 93 minutes to run through four rooms and go back to do some scrub work is a solid time window.

Overall, this vacuum really shines on hard floors, but I also liked it on rugs and carpet if you have a mix of these in your home. It has an auto-empty base with a bagless debris system, so you won’t need to worry about purchasing debris bags to empty the docking station. The only downside is that the vacuum can learn only a single map, so it doesn’t work for multiple floors of your home unless you’re game for it to remap every time (which takes only a couple minutes, so it’s not a horrible experience, but the vacuum will also want the base station lugged up or down the stairs too). The suction is also a mystery; Shark has declined to comment on the exact suction. Still, we’ve loved low-suction vacuums before, and the results have been great.

Recent findings suggest that this vacuum is one I refuse to part with, and while its retail price is technically $800, it's on sale enough in the $500 range that this has become the budget pick I'd easily recommend when it's on sale. The Roborock Qrevo 2 Pro is the newest patch to Roborock's more affordable Qrevo line, which went without updates for years. The Qrevo 2 Pro is cheaper than the Curv 2 that launched in January 2026, and it still packs a ton of power, great navigation, and the same handy app. It comes with 20,000 Pa of suction, a FlexiArm mop that does a better job of corner cleaning, and a reversible side brush to help dislodge corner debris. I love seeing the arm reach out and get all the edges and corners around my house, especially underneath cabinets in the kitchen and bathroom.

Recent findings suggest that the Qrevo 2 Pro also pulled ahead in some areas when compared against the similarly often-on-sale Eufy Omni C28. While the Eufy got itself stuck on cords in my bedroom, the Qrevo 2 Pro only attempted to eat cords without actually getting stuck on them. The Qrevo still isn't great at seeing small objects; it took my cat's toys for rides around the room, but they usually didn't get stuck or stop the vacuum. Both vacuums scored a 2 out of 3 on my Cheerio test, but the Qrevo 2 Pro got the harder fridge Cheerio with its FlexiArm mop. The Eufy did a little better on mopping, but neither vacuum did perfectly. I'm giving the Qrevo 2 Pro a 1.25 out of 2—one spill was just about gone, but the area around it was all slightly sticky, while the second spill was only half cleaned. It's hard to grade perfectly. It also occasionally leaves a little debris behind when it goes over thresholds that separate carpet from hard flooring, but it didn't have this glitch when transitioning onto rugs.

Sources indicate that this vacuum (and its base station) also looks good and is fairly quiet. (Except when it cleans on tile, which is a noisy experience as it travels across the grout divots. But it does a good job.) Both the base station and vacuum itself are quieter than the Eufy Omni C28, and it is especially pleasant if you let the Qrevo 2 Pro vacuum and mop separately. It takes longer than doing the combo cleans, but this vacuum pulled off doing both a separate vacuuming session and mopping of my massive first floor in two hours, which most vacuums still take for combo cleans.

Recent findings suggest that we've loved the app and navigation from Roborock for years, and it still stands out among its rivals in this area. The Roborock only struggles to navigate on a C-shaped table with long, thin, flat legs it can't see against my wood floors. Besides that it does a fantastic job navigating around all kinds of furniture and never runs into anything the way I've seen more expensive vacuums do. It can map multiple floors of my house too. Ultimately, it's a great, well-rounded vacuum for the price.

If the Roborock Qrevo isn't on sale, this Eufy is the next best thing. Former WIRED editor Adrienne So previously recommended Eufy’s older X10 Pro Omni as a great robot vacuum without spending too much, and Eufy released the Eufy Omni C28 in February this year with a similar set of features and price point. The Omni C28 comes with nearly double the suction power of the older model, a self-cleaning roller mop instead of mop pads, and retractable detangling brushes.

Industry observers note that it does a solid job mopping and vacuuming, but it has a shorter battery life, leaving it at only 37 percent after completing the four-room main floor of my house. This is a bit of a bummer, since this affordable vacuum can do multi-floor mapping. While it can store enough maps to clean all three levels of my home, it doesn’t have the battery life to do so. But it does charge fairly promptly, and I was able to still clean all three floors of my house in a single day—I just had to let it recharge a little at the base first. It went back up to 57 percent battery life after just 20 minutes in its docking station. It also tried to eat the cords near my bed, and luckily I was nearby to yank them free. If you get this vacuum, make sure your cords are clear of the vacuum's reach.

Industry observers note that with my corner Cheerio test, this vacuum also got two out of three Cheerios, but it missed the trickier fridge-corner Cheerio. This is the hardest spot to get into, so I’m not surprised, but it does mean you’ll have to check those corners more with this vacuum. The cherry juice spill test also highlighted similar results: The first spot it reached was cleaned completely, while the second spot, which had more time to dry, still had some sticky residue left behind.

Overall, though, it’s a good vacuum for the price, especially since it packs multi-floor mapping, the capability to mop and vacuum, and good results all around for a vacuum that’s already usually on sale for around or under $500.

There are a lot of great robot vacuums out there. Here are a few others we’ve tried and liked.

Dreame L60 Ultra for $1,000: This vacuum did a good all-around job and packs a ton of good features, including dual flex arms, the EasyLeap System that lets it move over almost-2-inch tall obstacles, and 35,000 Pa of suction. This is a great one to buy if you have tall thresholds in your home thanks to that lifting feature, but otherwise, you could get a smarter vacuum for a cheaper price. This vacuum does promise dirt detection, but I never noticed it delivering on that promise. Still, my Dreame long-term tester commented that it's leagues quieter than her older Dreame vacuum, so it's a good upgrade choice if you like Dreame and want something quieter.

According to recent reports, dreame X50 Ultra for $800: If you have pets that tend to make one area of your home particularly hair- or debris-covered, this is the vacuum to get. The Dreame X50 Ultra has tons of great features, including double-roll brushes, side wands for edge cleaning, and a large-capacity docking station, but the real standout is the AI that can notice extremely dirty areas. It’s the most effective dirt- and obstacle-identification system that former WIRED editor Adrienne So has tried, and it will even remind her which areas it needs to clean more often (for her, that’s near her dog’s bed).

Dyson Spot+Scrub Ai for $800: The Dyson Spot+Scrub Ai is a good robot vacuum overall, with a unique base station design that calls back to the Dyson stick vacuums and built-in AI to find spots and stains on your floor to scrub them away. It mostly worked, but I did prefer this feature in the Shark above, which has a similar starting retail price but is usually on sale. It’s also a little tall, so if you have builder-grade cabinets like I do, it might not be able to vacuum the toe kicks or underneath your Ikea furniture. (It got stuck underneath my Tolstad bed frame and was too tall to get underneath my Besta cabinet.).

According to recent reports, matic Robot Vacuum Bundle for $1,495: According to former WIRED editor Adrienne So, this vacuum is spectacular. It’s the only 10/10 rating she’s ever given a robot vacuum. Its six RGB infrared cameras do a great job making a 3D map, the single waste bag contains wet and dry debris, it does a great job cleaning toe kicks, and it was quiet enough to run without bothering So’s kids while they watched TV. That’s due to Matic’s lower suction power (only 3,200 Pa), but she didn’t notice any decrease in cleanliness as a result. It’s compact and square, giving it the ability to really get into corners. The only bummer is that it has expensive, proprietary waste bags. But those waste bags do have diaper salts, charcoal, and a HEPA filter, so you don’t have to replace the filters separately.

Industry observers note that narwal Flow for $849: WIRED’s Reviews team hasn’t always had success with Narwal’s vacuums, but when I tested this model late last year, I found it super easy to set up and get cleaning. I had no connectivity problems, installation was a breeze, and the app was easy to navigate. It did a good job cleaning my hard floors and rug, and even when I ran it right out of the box until it ran out of battery, it returned itself to its station to recharge and then resumed the task a few hours later, all on its own. The base station is also sleek and cute compared with the dark, bulky structures most have.

Industry observers note that roborock Saros 20 Flow for $1,300: If you're looking for something with serious suction, the Saros 20 Flow is my preferred choice out of Roborock's higher-power Saros line. I really like using it, and the roller mop does a good job mopping, but it only got one out of three Cheerios on my corner test and didn't manage to spot any stains on my floor, even with the promised built-in stain detection. It's the option I'd choose if you want a robot vacuum with great navigation and super-high suction (36,000 Pa) that won't deposit debris around the house like the Saros 20 tended to, but I think you'd be just as happy with a cheaper Roborock.

Roborock Qrevo Curv 2 for $1,000: This is another great option from Roborock and another part of the Qrevo line we've liked for years. The Qrevo Curv 2 came out in January and has similar strengths to the Qrevo 2 Pro above, but it has a roller mop called SpiraFlow instead of two individual mop pads. It also has similar struggles, with threshold debris and small objects being hard to spot. It's a good vacuum overall, and best on sale (which it often is!), but I'd pick my picks on sale over it.

It has been revealed that A robot vacuum is an automated vacuum, usually shaped like a round disc, that moves around your house to vacuum (and mop, as many models these days include mopping) on your behalf. You might’ve heard some refer to these devices as “Roombas,” which is the brand that made the concept popular, but today just about every cleaning brand—from high-end Dyson to affordable Bissell—makes some kind of robot vacuum. They come with either a charging station or a larger docking station that can self-empty.

There are a few things most robot vacuums will need to work properly:.

The Federal Communications Commission revealed in late July that foreign-produced advanced robotic devices will now be included on the FCC’s Covered List. That list includes communications equipment and services that are deemed to pose an unacceptable risk to the national security of the United States—including robot vacuums (and similar devices like robotic pool cleaners and lawn mowers). While it won’t ban any models already on the market that have FCC approval, we’ll likely see a huge decline in available latest models after this year. Models made in the US will be fine, but future vacuums from popular brands like Dreame, Eufy, Roborock, and more could be affected. For now, you'll still see vacuums launching from these brands, though, since FCC approval is given months ahead of product rolls out.

This decision comes from an interagency body in the White House executive branch called the National Security Determination, which has deemed automated robotic devices a security risk due to the data they collect, which could be used for surveillance and be remotely commandeered by “malign actors.” While the initial documentation describes humanoid robots and a recent case of a humanoid robot’s cybersecurity vulnerability to be remotely taken over, the official description of these robot devices will include robot vacuums and any devices meeting the following criteria:.

Sources indicate that overall, robot vacuums themselves aren’t banned, but new models from companies based outside the US won’t get FCC approval and can’t be sold in the US. You don’t need to stop using any robot vacuum you have, but if you’re in the market for a new one, it’s better to shop sooner before availability starts to decline—and prices are likely to rise as supply falls.

In a recent development, dyson R3 Nurovi Spot+Scrub UV for $1,200: Dyson's newest version of the Spot+Scrub has a UV light to help its AI spot stains, and I was happy to see those stains reported in the app, but I couldn't tell if the vacuum actually did more detailed cleaning in those areas. That aside, I wanted to love this vacuum more than I did. My issue with the vacuum is how it did in regular cleaning sessions: It left pieces of popcorn behind when vacuuming on my downstairs rugs, didn't seem to ever get close enough to my walls for any kind of edge cleaning, and was too tall to get underneath cabinets or basic Ikea furniture around my house (but still smacked into that furniture over and over again due to camera placement). It also got a zero on my corner Cheerio test, failing to even get the Cheerio that just sits near a chair leg. I haven't tested either of the cheaper upcoming Dyson robot vacuum options, but if this is how the best one does, I'm not inclined to.

Eufy S2 for $950: This robot vacuum has an intense-looking base station. However, I was disappointed it missed both the fridge and bookshelf Cheerios in my corner test, giving it only a one out of three. Both cherry stains were scrubbed away, but the floor near where the stains were felt sticky all over even with the stains ostensibly wiped away. It’s especially a bummer given the price point; it needed to do better to be worth such a high price tag.

It has been revealed that iRobot Roomba Max 705 Combo for $800: The name Roomba is synonymous with robot vacuums for many people, but it’s actually a specific line made by iRobot. I really liked both the high-end look of the Max 705 Combo (not to be confused with the cheaper Max 705) and the overall job it did mopping and cleaning my floors. The app is great since it indicates you a map of where the robot went, and it’ll also show you a little itinerary of which rooms it’s doing in what order. However, setup and any resetting you need to do is a long process, so be ready to commit and troubleshoot when you unbox it. My long-term tester has also reported that its mopping abilities have not improved over the six months it's been running in her house, but it does best with vacuuming and carpet.

iRobot Roomba Max 875 Combo With ThermaMist for $799: As Roomba’s new top-line robot vacuum and mop, this model features 35,000 Pa of suction, as well as hot steam to pretreat stuck-on stains. However, what really sold me was the “no pre-clean pickup” advertised on the box. I’ve got pet toys, my teen’s sports equipment and shoes all over the floor, cords, and loose rugs; other robot vacuums I’ve tried have struggled with my household. The Max 875, however, moved through my house with ease—in fact, I was quite impressed with how well it powered through even the toughest robovac challenges, like shoelaces and a maze of tucked-in chairs around a table. It did fine on pedestrian stains on my LVP floors, like spilled coffee, but even with the ThermaMist and repeated returns to the scene, the 875 Combo couldn’t fully clean an area with dried wet cat food. Setup was also pretty buggy—I followed the manual, but the vacuum took off before I could add it to the app and map my house, trying to clean a random area on 14 percent battery life. It would then return to the dock station, charge for five minutes, and repeat this process for well over an hour. When I did get it connected to the app, it mentioned it needed an patch but was unable to download it. I eventually got it to work by factory-resetting the machine and starting all over, but this process took more patience than I’d expect at this price point. —Kat Merck.

Industry observers note that iRobot Roomba Plus 678 Combo Robot + AutoWash Dock for $599: Like its fancier sibling, the Max 875 above, the Plus 678 had a bit of a buggy setup process that required several attempts and a factory reset. The Plus 678 also has the Max 875’s AI-powered stain pretreatment (though without the ThermaMist steam) and 30,000 Pa of suction for Roomba’s fresh “SealForce” technology, which lowers a skirt around carpets to suction deeper into the pile. I tested this with three different types of rugs—a regular-pile wool rug, a loose washable rug, and a low-pile faux fur rug. It did well on the first two, but failed on the third, becoming fully stuck. (Most vacuums can’t handle this rug, so I don’t exactly fault it for this.) Other than the setup mishaps—which included false “brush roller failure” messages and a mapping attempt that left it turning around in circles in the middle of an open room for 20 minutes—this is a serviceable mop-vac with a feature list that’s hard to fault at this price. —Kat Merck.

It has been revealed that iRobot Roomba Plus 575 Combo Robot + AutoWash Dock for $499: After hearing about the futuristic Roomba growing up, I was excited to see one in action. During setup, I found that the battery cover unscrewed, but assumed it was intentional since no screws were included. It soon fell off, so I taped it; days later, it came off during cleaning and got lost, leaving the battery and cords exposed to debris and the wet mop. Not great. From the start, it struggled to map my home. Cleaning requires app routines, which I didn’t love, as sometimes I just wanted to be able to click a single room and go without having to create another routine. The routines were often ignored or stopped midway. A mop pad fell off on every single run, forcing me to retrace the machine’s path to find it in my home. It also got caught on cords and repeatedly tried to climb my cat tree’s base, getting stuck perpetually spinning until I had to manually move it. Edge cleaning was nonexistent; there was so much cat hair and dust near where the floor met the wall. After a month, it threw up and scattered debris whenever it crossed the ¾-inch thresholds to the bathroom, kitchen, and bedroom, so afterward I had to vacuum the mess it created—defeating the purpose. —Molly Higgins.

Mova P10 Pro Ultra Gen2 for $360: This robot vacuum was solid, and especially did a good job with cleaning corners (it got a 2 out of 3 on the corner test, capturing both the stool and fridge Cheerios), but it did a poor job scrubbing away the cherry juice for my stain tests. One of the two stains was almost entirely left behind, and overall on casual runs of the vacuum it didn’t feel as if my floors were super clean. Still, if you’re looking for good corner cleaning, and carpets more than hard-floor deep cleaning, this is a solid robot vacuum for the price.

Roborock Saros 20 for $990: WIRED reviewer Adrienne So was mostly happy with this robot vacuum, as was I. She noticed the super-high suction (it hits 36,000 Pa) actually caused more debris to be left behind on her hard floors when it passed over thresholds; I didn't have this glitch with the thresholds in my home, but instead I found debris on my hard floors immediately after having this vacuum clean them, with no threshold required. It also only got a one out of three in my Cheerio test, which isn't great for such an expensive vacuum.

According to recent reports, tapo RV50 Pro Omni for $400: After testing several robovacs that made me want to chuck them out the window, I had high hopes for Tapo’s newly introduced model that was released this summer. It promised over four hours of run time, dual-laser obstacle avoidance, DeepEdge mopping for corners and edges, and automatic floor detection to keep mops off carpets. But during more than two weeks of testing, it never mapped my home correctly or fully cleaned it. It couldn’t cross the ¾-inch raised thresholds into my kitchen or bathroom, and it mapped my bedroom but detected a phantom obstacle and cleaned only the 2-foot entryway. My kitchen, bathroom, and bedroom were never fully cleaned during testing. It’d be heading for the dock to wash mops or empty them and would forget to do the hall next or finish the living room and begin charging again. About half the time, the app asked me to map my home again, apparently forgetting the previous day’s map. During mapping, it sometimes started cleaning, got lost, and then announced it couldn’t find its dock, leaving me to locate and return it. When vacuuming, it sometimes left the mops at the station, returned for them, forgot, and began charging, thus ending its task. Not once did it successfully vacuum and mop my whole home. Online reviews are glowing, so perhaps I got a dud—but this experience was enough to make me want to clean by hand instead. —Molly Higgins.

Recent findings suggest that I test all robot vacuums in my three-story townhouse, where they clean across luxury vinyl plank (LVP); tile; carpet; and a large, low-pile rug. I have a dining table and four barstools to navigate, and both a cat and a child who create daily messes. I run the vacuum at least three times across the main floors of my home to assess its overall performance and note any recurring issues or errors it encounters. I do pick up my son’s toys, but I like to watch how the robot navigates the various chair legs and side tables throughout my home, and whether it sucks up the power cords beside my bed. I also like to see how much battery life is left after a run is complete on each level of my home.

My corner test, using three Cheerios in three corner (or cornerlike) spots.

I also set up an obstacle course of sorts. The first one is the corner test, created by three Cheerios placed in three tricky corners on the middle floor of my home: one in the corner of an Ikea Billy bookshelf toe kick, one underneath my countertops next to the fridge, and one next to a barstool chair leg. It’s how I test how well each robot vacuum gets into corners and underneath cabinetry.

My spill test, with two spots of cherry juice on the floor.

I also create intentional spills for these vacuums to clean up. I use maraschino cherry juice to create two spill spots, then use a paper towel to smear and thin the stain to better replicate a spill you might not have seen on your floors. Many robot vacuums have AI that promises to detect these kinds of stains, but so far, no vacuum has stopped and scrubbed both spots on its first try.

Can You Use Robot Vacuums on All Kinds of Floors?

You can, especially since there are so many mopping models now to better clean hard flooring. You can use these devices on anything from hardwood to LVP and tile, though I wouldn't recommend leaving smaller rugs out for these autonomous gadgets to get stuck on. Large, set rugs are fine, but bathroom and kitchen mats or any thin, easily moved rugs should be cleared out of the way and put in the wash instead of vacuumed by your robot vac.

How Often Do You Need to Maintain Your Robot Vacuum?

In a recent development, taking good care of your robot vacuum will help it last. Here’s the debris-removal process you should follow for each robot vacuum style.

In a recent development, make sure to review your robot vacuum’s manual for any other steps the manufacturer recommends you take regularly to keep the vacuum running for as long as possible. Many brands also have replacement parts, so you can swap out individual pieces like brushes without needing an entirely new vacuum.

Do I Still Need a Regular Vacuum if I Have a Robot Vacuum?

I recommend keeping some kind of vacuum on hand, though that can vary based on your home. If you have stairs, you’ll definitely still want a hand vacuum or stick vacuum that can easily maneuver and clean your staircase, while pet owners might want a vacuum that can clean upholstery. I prefer my Dyson stick vacuums for a good carpet clean, but your mileage may vary depending on your preferences. Either way, I think everyone needs a companion vacuum of some kind with a robot vacuum.

Do You Need a Self-Emptying Dock?

You don’t need it, but a self-emptying dock makes using a robot vacuum much easier. You aren’t fumbling with debris every time it runs, and having a single bag to remove or a bin to empty is much easier than pulling debris out of the vacuum itself. I’d even recommend choosing a stick vac with a self-emptying dock, as it just makes the whole experience so much easier.

How Does WIRED Obtain Robot Vacuums? What Happens When We’re Done Testing?

Almost all the robot vacuums we test are provided to us as press samples with the understanding that there is no guarantee of coverage or type of coverage. Most companies don’t want a used vacuum back, so we either donate them locally or have the top performers long-term tested to see how they last.

FAA pauses installation of new routers after ground stop

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The Federal Aviation Administration mentioned Tuesday it would pause the installation of new routers after problems with the technology led the agency to concern a rare nationwide ground stop on Friday.
  • Tens of thousands of flights were affected by the ground stop, which halted departing flights for more than four hours.
  • Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy noted Sunday that an overloaded router installed in southern Arkansas as part of an upgrade to a system overseen by L3Harris Technologies appeared to overwhelm systems that feed radar and other data for air traffic control.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Federal Aviation Administration mentioned Tuesday it would pause the installation of new routers after problems with the technology led the agency to concern a rare nationwide ground stop on Friday.

Tens of thousands of flights were affected by the ground stop, which halted departing flights for more than four hours. It was the longest halt to U.S. flight departures since 9/11.

Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy noted Sunday that an overloaded router installed in southern Arkansas as part of an upgrade to a system overseen by L3Harris Technologies appeared to overwhelm systems that feed radar and other data for air traffic control.

The Wall Street Journal first reported the news about the pause.

The FAA and Department of Transportation have mentioned L3Harris was working to convert the communications network from copper wires to fiber optic.

Democratic members of the Senate Committee on Commerce, Science and Transportation this week asked the FAA and the Department of Transportation for clarity on what went wrong.

It has been revealed that "Identifying the device that failed does not establish why it failed," the senators wrote in a statement. "Modernization cannot come at the expense of operational safety.".

The agencies have said they are working to figure out the root cause of the glitch and have reiterated that there is no indication of a cyberattack or outside threat.

In a recent development, the senators also asked for a briefing with the FAA, L3Harris and Juniper Networks, which is making the latest devices, by Monday. They asked the companies to lay out why the operational systems lacked sufficient redundancy and answer other questions about what led to the outage.

CNBC has reached out to L3Harris and Juniper Networks for comment.

In a recent development, duffy on Friday called for Congress to approve $50 billion in funding for upgrades to the aging U.S. air traffic control system, more than he has previously asked for. Democratic lawmakers pushed back on the request, citing unspent money from existing funding, which includes Congress' approval last year of $12.5 billion for airport and air traffic control improvements over five years.

Senate Commerce Chair Ted Cruz, R-Texas, mentioned Tuesday that he thinks there will be support for air traffic control modernization, but that the allocation should be specifically for safety upgrades.

Recent findings suggest that "I don't think the full $50 billion will be funded," he stated. "Some of that is not safety related, but we just discussed there, and what I expressed is that the request needs to be focused on safety modernization.".

Recent findings suggest that duffy dismissed the idea that the router glitch had to do with the introduction of artificial intelligence tools and said it was "completely unfounded" because the AI system is not in communication with the defective router. He added that the FBI is helping to investigate the root cause of the issue.

Aging equipment and a shortage of air traffic controllers have for years angered airline executives, who have complained about the cost of resulting disruptions.

  • At a press conference in Berlin on Tuesday, Interior Minister Alexander Dobrindt, Family Affairs Minister Karin Prien and Justice Minister Stefanie Hubig released the latest figures on crimes that specifically target women: whether within families and intimate relationships, in public or online.
  • In contrast to the statistics pertaining to crime overall, which have remained the same or increased only slightly, reports of crimes against women have increased.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The German government has presented some grim statistics with regard to misogyny, rape, violence and murder, with reported cases of domestic violence at an all-time high.

At a press conference in Berlin on Tuesday, Interior Minister Alexander Dobrindt, Family Affairs Minister Karin Prien and Justice Minister Stefanie Hubig released the latest figures on crimes that specifically target women: whether within families and intimate relationships, in public or online.

In contrast to the statistics pertaining to crime overall, which have remained the same or increased only slightly, reports of crimes against women have increased.

"Behind all these terrible numbers lie individual stories, people and particularly women and girls, whose lives are severely affected by these acts of violence," said Dobrindt.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Recent findings suggest that in 2025, some 280,000 people were victims of physical abuse in their own homes, a 2.8% increase compared to the previous year. Over 70% of the victims were female. Each hour, 16 women are subjected to physical abuse behind closed doors.

The male victims included boys who had been assaulted by their fathers.

The number of misogynistic hate crimes has also risen dramatically, by almost 50%, to 819 cases.

Industry observers note that "The figures show us what it can mean to be a woman in Germany," said Hubig. "It can mean being killed by one's partner or ex-partner. Being a woman can also mean being physically abused by one's partner or ex-partner in one's own home. Being a woman can mean that one's sexual autonomy is brutally disregarded.".

It has been revealed that according to the latest findings, both perpetrators and victims are getting younger. In 2025, nearly half of all female victims of sexual offenses were under the age of 18. And the number of incidents of online violence against women and girls rose by 15.7%. This includes the unauthorized sharing of videos and photos, verbal abuse, manipulation of images, threats and online blackmail, as well as cyberstalking.

Because many perpetrators and victims are still in their teens, Prien, who is also minister for education, stated the government wanted to focus primarily on schools, which she explained should become places of prevention.

In a recent development, "Ultimately, we need to bring about a change in people's mindsets, especially those of men. That will be the deciding factor in the end," she remarked.

According to recent reports, over the weekend, Justice Minister Hubig had already revealed that in future all femicides, the intentional killing of girls and women because of their gender, would be classified as murders. Currently, such crimes are often classified as manslaughter, for which the penalty is less severe than for murder.

Hubig told German broadcaster ZDF that it was increasingly common that femicides be described as family tragedies or as domestic dramas revolving around jealousy and then classified as manslaughter.

According to recent reports, martina Link, the vice president of the Federal Criminal Police Office, was also at the press conference in Berlin. She called for everybody to pay closer attention to the issue, within their own families, neighborhoods or at work.

"Violence against women is not a private matter," she mentioned. "Not in our immediate surroundings nor in the digital world.".

She also pointed out that when it came to sexual offenses and domestic violence, only about 5-10% of cases were reported.

This article was originally written in German.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Hanna Hattab has refereed in a number of competitions run by the Asian Football Confederation.

Claims that a referee was drunk during an Asian Football Confederation (AFC) Champions League Two match are "entirely unfounded", officials say.

Syrian referee Hanna Hattab was replaced at half-time of the match between Iran's Gol Gohar and Al Jazira of the United Arab Emirates.

Reports claimed Gol Gohar staff accused the referee of being drunk following what has been described as some erratic decision-making in the first half.

Iranian news agency ISNA quoted one club official as saying: "The referee was not in a normal state," and suggesting they would not have played on had the referee not been removed.

Accusations of drunkenness were also widely shared on social media.

But Hattab, who is part of the AFC's elite refereeing group, has released a statement denying the allegation, saying he has been defamed and threatening legal action.

The fourth official took over for the second half, with Al Jazira winning the match.

Hattab stated he will be "issuing an official statement that clarifies all the details and facts related to what happened".

Omani sports journalist Issa Remarked, who covers Asian competitions, claimed on social media that what happened to Hattab was "due to a drop in his blood sugar, which caused him to lose concentration and focus".

"He underwent a medical examination after the match and was not intoxicated, contrary to what has been circulating.".

In their statement on the match, which was played in Asia's second tier continental competition, the Syrian Football Association backed Hattab.

"Following an assessment of his health, it has been confirmed - contrary to various claims circulating on social media - that the reports regarding his situation are entirely unfounded," they wrote.

"The Committee reiterates its unwavering support for him and is committed to thoroughly investigating all details and circumstances surrounding the incident.".

#152143. Latest Update: Musk's Twitter promised a purge of blue check marks. Instead he singled out the New York Times
