Industry News: Hera spacecraft gets 1st up-close look at stadium-sized hole punched in asteroid by NASA DART mission

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (770 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Space

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • NASA's DART Earth-defense mission punched a stadium-sized hole in a distant asteroid, and we have seen it up close for the first time thanks to the Hera spacecraft.
  • NASA's DART (Double Asteroid Redirection Test) mission made history on Sept.
  • According to recent reports, now, the spacecraft has revealed that DART flattened one face of Dimorphos with a stadium-sized crater and set it tumbling chaotically.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

NASA's DART Earth-defense mission punched a stadium-sized hole in a distant asteroid, and we have seen it up close for the first time thanks to the Hera spacecraft.

NASA's DART (Double Asteroid Redirection Test) mission made history on Sept. 26, 2022, when it slammed into Dimorphos, the small moonlet of the much larger asteroid Didymos. The mission tested if such an impact could be deployed to divert an asteroid on a collision course with Earth. Scientists have known for some time that this deflection attempt was successful; the system's orbit around the sun was lengthened by 33 minutes, but the European Space Agency's (ESA) Hera mission launched in October 2024 to travel the 120 million miles (194 million kilometers) to the Didymos system to observe the effect of the DART impact in greater detail.

According to recent reports, now, the spacecraft has revealed that DART flattened one face of Dimorphos with a stadium-sized crater and set it tumbling chaotically. The impact also appears to have blasted out hundreds of previously unknown boulders that are now circling the binary asteroids.

"Scientists debated whether Dimorphos had sustained an impact crater, changed its shape, or stayed the same," Hera principal investigator Patrick Michel, Director of Research at the Observatoire de la Côte d'Azur, said in a statement.

"Much to our surprise, the answer turns out to be all three at once! The face struck by DART has been flattened into an impact crater the size of a sports stadium, which extends across the asteroid's entire width.".

Michael Kueppers, ESA's Hera mission scientist, detailed some of the changes to the impacted moonlet seen by the spacecraft: "As Hera returned more images, it became clear that the DART impact has left Dimorphos tumbling wildly in its orbit.

"Another big surprise is that Hera is showing that the asteroids are surrounded by hundreds of orbiting boulders, just a few meters in size.".

Recent findings suggest that it wasn't all change for Dimorphos. Hera discovered that the boulder fields covering the regions of the moonlet not impacted look just like they did when DART imaged it in 2022.

Hera isn't finished with Didymos and its moonlet. The ESA spacecraft is at the moment in a rectangular orbit around the asteroid binary system, using its thrusters to maintain a distance of around 18.6 miles (30 kilometers). This allows Hera to continue observing Didymos and Dimorphos.

Recent findings suggest that hera will soon come to within around 8 miles (13 km) of the asteroids, capturing even more detailed images of the space rocks. Following this, it will deploy two showbox-sized CubeSats, which will get even closer to the asteroids.

The CubeSat Juventas will use low-frequency radar to probe the interior of Dimorphos, the first time this has ever been done for an asteroid, and will eventually attempt to land on the moonlet to measure its gravity. Meanwhile, the Milani CubeSat will prospect asteroid materials and dust around the Didymos system.

Together, Hera and its CubeSats will more precisely determine the mass of Dimorphos, which, when combined with information about the orbital change of the system, will be crucial in planning missions to deflect threatening asteroids.

In a recent development, hera's observations were revealed on Wednesday (Nov. 25) at the dinosaur hall of the Museum für Naturkunde Berlin, Germany. That location isn't a coincidence: It is a stark reminder of why this planetary defense mission is so vital. Especially if humanity doesn't want to go the way of the dinosaurs, whose rule on Earth ended when an asteroid fell from the sky."Sixty-six million years ago, an asteroid impact changed the course of life on Earth. Today, for the first time in history, humanity is validating how to prevent such an event from happening again," Hera mission manager Ian Carnelli explained. "NASA's DART mission demonstrated that we can change an asteroid's orbit. Hera is now revealing what happened to the asteroid itself. "By combining these two missions, humanity is taking a decisive step towards making asteroid deflection a reliable tool for protecting our planet.".

It has been revealed that robert Lea is a science journalist in the U.K. whose articles have been published in Physics World, New Scientist, Astronomy Magazine, All About Space, Newsweek and ZME Science. He also writes about science communication for Elsevier and the European Journal of Physics. Rob holds a bachelor of science degree in physics and astronomy from the U.K.’s Open University. Iordanescu ready for Watford 'challenge'

📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1046 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Edward Iordandescu is the first Romanian to manage in the top four tiers of English football.
  • New Watford boss Edward Iordanescu says he has inherited a "challenge" but also "an opportunity" as the club seeks to pull away from the Championship relegation zone.
  • The 48-year-old has replaced Alessio Dionisi, who was sacked on Sunday after only five months in charge, following a run of seven defeats in 10 league games.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Edward Iordandescu is the first Romanian to manage in the top four tiers of English football.

New Watford boss Edward Iordanescu says he has inherited a "challenge" but also "an opportunity" as the club seeks to pull away from the Championship relegation zone.

The 48-year-old has replaced Alessio Dionisi, who was sacked on Sunday after only five months in charge, following a run of seven defeats in 10 league games.

Iordanescu became Watford's sixth new boss in less than 18 months and is the 25th manager since the Pozzo family took over the club in 2012.

He will take charge of the Hornets for the first time on Saturday when they travel to bottom club Derby County.

The Romanian met the media for the first time on Friday, and set out his vision for his tenure.

The Watford job is Iordanescu's first since leaving Legia Warsaw in October 2025, having won the Polish Super Cup with them last season.

It is the 10th managerial post of his 15-year coaching career, which has taken in Bulgarian club CSKA Sofia as well as Steaua Bucharest and Cluj - who he guided to the Romanian title and two domestic cups after joining midway through the 2020-21 season.

He also spent two and a half years in charge of Romania, guiding them to the last 16 of Euro 2024, where they were beaten by the Netherlands.

However, in his first job in English football, he inherits a Watford side three points above the drop zone and facing a fight for their second-tier status.

"I'm proud more than anything else and I'm honoured and happy to be here, but I'm also very aware of the challenge in front of me," Iordanescu told BBC Three Counties Radio.

Recent findings suggest that "I don't want to make promises. I know the fans are not happy in this moment, but also I know that my words are not enough to bring them back, so they wait for facts. We need that, but of course there is a lot of work to do, there is a process in front of us and I hope we make the next steps right away.

"For me it's a challenge but at the same time it's an opportunity and I want to transform this opportunity into something good for the club, for the fans. This is the most important [thing].".

Prior to the dismissal of Dionisi, former Watford player Tom Ince - who left the club at the end of the 2025-26 season - told the BBC's 72+ Podcast there was "so much control away from the manager" at Vicarage Road.

While Ince, now at League Two side Tranmere Rovers, added his respect of positives of chairman Gino Pozzo's practises, he is not alone in speaking out about the board's influence.

Former England boss Sam Allardyce stated he turned down the Watford job in 2019 after claiming he was told how the side should play and which players should be in the XI.

But Iordandescu revealed that is not his expectation.

In a recent development, "I know my borders and I know my responsibilities." he said. "I'm in this club with a lot of quality people, professionals, people that know, understand, in detail, football, but starting yesterday I'm the number one in the technical side.

"I don't believe there's somebody here in the club that can overcome the coach, taking the technical knowledge, so it will be my responsibility, but also the technical part will be my decision all the time.".

Pioneer or coach-eater? The complex world of Pozzo's Watford.

From a purely statistical perspective, Watford's laboured start to the season under Dionisi could be credited to one key deficiency.

The Hornets have scored the fewest goals in the Championship, with only 13 in their 17 matches so far.

However, Iordanescu remarked his primary objective was not to thrill, but to win.

He said: "I always prefer to win 1-0 than 4-2. One-nil means you have an organised team, a team with some responsibility to engage 100% and to give everything for the result.

"So for me the priority is not to score more goals - [it is] to start to be organised, to start to act and react together on the pitch, to start to understand that the mindset should be a little bit different than what it was until now and to start to be efficient.

"In time we will see about scoring more goals, definitely every coach wants the team to score as much as possible.".

Edward Iordanescu: My initiative for Watford.

Iordanescu also appeared to confirm he was in talks about taking over while Dionisi was still in charge.

It was reported on 12 November that the Hertfordshire club were in talks with him, but Dionisi, who had only been appointed in June, remained in charge across the international break and for Saturday's 4-0 defeat at Sheffield United.

The Italian was sacked on Sunday, with Iordanescu appointed on Wednesday.

Iordanescu said he had "asked for time" from the Watford hierachy before accepting the role.

He noted: "I wanted to understand very clearly the objectives, the targets, so when I gave the final response, I was aware of everything.

Recent findings suggest that "I'm here, I'm enthusiastic, I'm positive, I'm confident we can do good things together, and the thing which I count most on is the potential of this very young team. One of the youngest teams in the league.".

But Iordanescu also took time to pay tribute to his predecessor.

"He [Dionisi] definitely worked hard," noted Iordanescu.

In a recent development, "He did and left good things, very good things, already I saw many of them. But in football when things don't run the way you want and when the results are not backing up your work, it's difficult.

"I know he is a coach that put a lot of heart in his work and thank him for the good things that he did, and also tried to achieve here.".

The task at hand now for Iordanescu is to succeed where Dionisi, and so many other Hornets bosses since their Premier League relegation in 2022, could not.

Chromosome ‘glue’ could boost fertility by stabilizing ageing eggs

📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (781 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Chromosomes are held together with protein structures called cohesins, but these diminish with age.Credit: Power and Syred/Science Photo Library.
  • In a recent development, researchers have engineered a ‘molecular glue’ that can stabilize chromosomes in ageing mouse eggs1.
  • In a recent development, chromosomes in animal eggs are held together by protein structures called cohesins.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Chromosomes are held together with protein structures called cohesins, but these diminish with age.Credit: Power and Syred/Science Photo Library.

In a recent development, researchers have engineered a ‘molecular glue’ that can stabilize chromosomes in ageing mouse eggs1. They say their artificial cohesion system could pave the way for improved fertility treatments for women over the age of 35.

In a recent development, chromosomes in animal eggs are held together by protein structures called cohesins. These help to ensure that chromosomes divide correctly during the process of cell division. But the level of cohesins declines as women age, which can cause chromosomes to separate early and be distributed incorrectly. The resulting eggs can have too many or too few chromosomes, a condition known as aneuploidy, which is a cause of infertility, failed in-vitro-fertilization (IVF) treatments and early pregnancy loss, particularly in women who are more than 35 years old.

In a recent development, to prevent this premature separation of chromosomes in eggs, Melina Schuh, a biochemist at Max Planck Institute for Multidisciplinary Sciences in Göttingen, Germany, and her colleagues designed an artificial system called TALhesin. The system uses engineered proteins that attach to regions of the chromosome in which cohesin is usually present, these proteins then bind to one another.

Many groups are trying to understand cohesin because it diminishes as women age, affecting fertility, states Bettina Mihalas, a reproductive biologist at the University of New South Wales in Sydney, Australia, but this is the first approach to replace the protein’s function with an engineered system. “It’s a very creative, well-engineered and well-thought-out approach,” she says.

The findings were published in Science1 on 26 November.

Industry observers note that the researchers injected messenger RNA that encoded the engineered proteins into immature mouse eggs. The mouse eggs then produced the proteins. Using fluorescence microscopy imaging, the researchers confirmed that the TALhesin proteins attached to chromosome regions in which natural cohesin is normally lost.

The artificial system reduced the frequency of early chromosome separation in older mice aged 13 months, 17 months and 20 months compared with untreated eggs. In 17-month-old mice, the proportion of eggs without any premature chromosome-separation errors increased from 46.7% to 74.1% in those treated with TALhesin, similar to what is observed in eggs from young mice.

It has been revealed that chromatids — the two identical halves formed by a replicating chromosome — must separate at the right time during cell division. To enable this, the researchers added a ‘molecular scissor’ into their artificial system. This switched off the artificial cohesion system at the appropriate time.

The team has adapted the system to deliver engineered proteins that attach to regions of human chromosomes in which cohesin is usually present.

According to recent reports, experiments in donated human eggs revealed that the TALhesin proteins accumulated in these regions. The researchers also found that chromosomes with high levels of the engineered proteins tended to have smaller distances between chromatids. This demonstrates that the TALhesin system holds the chromosomes together.

The Best MagSafe Wallets for Your Everyday Carry (2026)

📅 20 Nov 2024 | ⏱️ 14 min read (2888 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: WIRED

⏱️ ~14 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The best MagSafe wallets are compact, slim, and svelte, and they attach securely to your iPhone (or MagSafe-compatible case).
  • Read our MagSafe guides for more useful accessory recommendations, including the Best MagSafe Accessories, Best MagSafe Power Banks, Best MagSafe Wireless Chargers, and Best MagSafe Grips.
  • Updated November 2026: I’ve added upcoming wallets to our honorable mentions section and removed discontinued products.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The best MagSafe wallets are compact, slim, and svelte, and they attach securely to your iPhone (or MagSafe-compatible case). They are handy if you only want to carry a few cards, like your work badge or train fare. MagSafe wallets are also great for anyone who wants to travel light and forgo a traditional wallet entirely. We’ve tested dozens, and our favorites are below.

Read our MagSafe guides for more useful accessory recommendations, including the Best MagSafe Accessories, Best MagSafe Power Banks, Best MagSafe Wireless Chargers, and Best MagSafe Grips.

Updated November 2026: I’ve added upcoming wallets to our honorable mentions section and removed discontinued products. I’ve also checked for accuracy throughout.

Recent findings suggest that magSafe is Apple’s magnetic technology built into the iPhone 12, iPhone 13, iPhone 14, iPhone 15, iPhone 16 (excluding the iPhone 16e), iPhone 17, iPhone 18 Pro, and iPhone Duo. It features a hidden ring of magnets on the back of the phone and was developed to create a faster, more precise wireless charging system. Those magnets also connect to accessories such as external batteries, car mounts, and wallets.

If you use a case on your iPhone, make sure it’s also MagSafe (the case will have a ring of magnets inside). This will ensure a proper connection with MagSafe accessories. If you use a non-MagSafe case, the connection will be very weak, and MagSafe products may just slide off your iPhone. We have lots of case recommendations in our guides:.

Recent findings suggest that when buying a wallet, make sure it supports MagSafe or Qi2 connections. The product description should indicate this prominently. Qi2 is the wireless charging standard, and all MagSafe iPhones support Qi2. Android phones now also support Qi2, and some have magnets inside, like the Google Pixel 10 and Pixel 11 series (Google calls it Pixelsnap).

MagSafe wallets use the same ring of magnets that lets them snap directly onto the back of the iPhone or a MagSafe- or supported Qi2 case. This gives the wallet a strong and secure hold on your device. The wallets we’ve included in this guide all have the MagSafe seal of approval.

Recent findings suggest that apple first introduced MagSafe for its iPhones in 2020. The following models support the technology:.

Do MagSafe Wallets Work With Android Phones?

To use a MagSafe wallet with an Android phone (or the iPhone 16e), you’ll need to use a MagSafe case. Several case manufacturers have started adding a ring of magnets to Android phone cases to bring the same magnetic experience native to iPhones.

Will a MagSafe Wallet Demagnetize My Credit Card?

According to recent reports, no, MagSafe will not demagnetize your credit cards. Credit cards have magnetic stripe encoding strong enough to resist demagnetization, and the MagSafe wallets in this guide include a built-in shield designed to keep your cards safe. However, you may run into challenges with hotel key cards and some gift cards. Keep those away as a precaution.

Recent findings suggest that I use a MagSafe wallet every day as my primary wallet. I check that it snaps firmly onto the iPhone or MagSafe case—and that it doesn’t slide off when I take my phone out of my pocket, bag, or jacket. I also make sure cards fit well in the sleeve and don’t fall out. I only recommend wallets that feel durable, are easy to use, and can hold the standard amount of cards (at least two to three). I occasionally call on my fellow WIRED reviewers for long-term testing or to check out fresh models.

UAG’s Metropolis MagSafe wallet is on the spendier side, but you won’t be replacing it in a year or two. It is lightweight yet robust with Kevlar construction. There’s a large slot on the back that can hold up to three cards, and you can unfold the wallet and store an additional three (or cash) inside. It also pulls double duty as a stand if you need to prop up your phone, and you can orient your phone in landscape or portrait mode. —Molly Higgins.

Smartish’s MagSafe wallet makes me wish all wallets had a slot on the side to push out the cards. I never had to take it off my phone to access cards. Just give the spacious side opening a little push with your thumb, and the cards slide out. My cards remained secure, and I never had an issue with them falling out. It’s made of vegan leather, and Smartish offers a few fun designs. —Brenda Stolyar.

Industry observers note that this luxe, super-thin leather MagSafe wallet from Nomad has Apple’s Find My feature built in, so you can easily locate it in the Find My app if it’s misplaced. That does mean you need to charge the wallet, but don’t worry, there's no proprietary cable here. Instead, the wallet can be wirelessly charged on any MagSafe or Qi2 charger; once it’s fully charged, the battery lasts for five months. Easy peasy.

It’s made from vegetable-tanned Horween leather with a polycarbonate frame, and it can hold up to four cards. (A less expensive version that uses Nomad's Camino leather is also available.) It looks classy, and it’s great for anyone with a tendency to lose things. —Molly Higgins.

Note that Nomad also sells a dedicated tracker card, which can add Find My to any wallet but will take up valuable space in a MagSafe version.

It has been revealed that I love this wallet from Moft, which is compatible with Apple Find My, so you always know where it is. It’s relatively standard-looking, but it has a built-in tripod, which came in handy numerous times when I wanted to film a quick outfit check or take a group photo. It raises your phone camera to 8 inches high, and the wallet is very sturdy, so you can dial in the right angle. It works in landscape or portrait orientation. With space for two cards, it isn’t the roomiest but is rich in features. —Louryn Strampe.

Industry observers note that you can always rely on Casetify for unique designs. Its Snappy MagSafe wallet is available in various styles and colors. It’s slim, durable, and sleek—the illustrations haven’t faded after months of use. It’s made from vegan leather (aka plastic), but Casetify uses BioVeg, derived from recycled polyester and vegetable oil from non-food and GMO-free corn crops.

It can hold up to three cards, and there’s a built-in shield that protects them from magnetic damage. My only gripe is that it can be a little difficult to pull the cards out when the wallet is attached to your phone or case. I typically have to detach it and use the opening from the back to slide out the cards. —Brenda Stolyar.

In a recent development, ridge’s metal MagSafe wallet feels solid and high-quality. A few of us tested it, and it reliably held our setups, including one tester’s daily carry of eight cards plus a thicker tracking card. The magnets could be stronger, but Ridge does sell a strengthening tray that might be useful if you’re concerned.

This wallet can be a little weird to use at first, but you build up muscle memory quickly. There’s a finger slot for pushing cards out, and you slide them back in on the opposite side. Ridge also includes a Torx screwdriver and extra screws, which are useful for switching out the plates, adding or subtracting room for cards, or adding on accessories like the brand’s wallet chain or cash strap. —Louryn Strampe.

Most MagSafe wallets are designed to hold just a few cards, but I love the Moft Snap Field because it can hold so much more. You get plenty of storage space for cards—technically up to eight cards, though more reasonably seven—alongside a dedicated slot for an extra SIM card and a SIM card ejector.

That extra room already puts the Snap Field a step ahead of most other MagSafe wallets, but you can also store just about anything you want inside. It uses a folding design held together by magnets, so you can rapidly throw in cash, coins, or paper cards. Regardless of what you store inside, you can easily get to your cards with a pull tab. And, if all of that wasn’t enough, the backing that attaches to your phone can pop out and function as a kickstand. —Jacob Roach.

Sources indicate that ESR’s MagSafe wallet isn’t bulky, but it also isn’t so thin that it feels insubstantial. It doubles as a kickstand and sticks to my phone reliably. There’s space for five cards—three in the external pockets, plus another two on the inside. I really like the clear window that keeps my ID separate and handy to flash when I get carded. This wallet is simple, but that’s the beauty of it, and it’s affordable to boot. If you want something basic, it’s a good option to consider. Just keep in mind that the included RFID-blocking card probably isn’t necessary. —Louryn Strampe.

Recent findings suggest that casely’s wallet is made of hard silicone, so it’s slightly heavier and thicker than the other ones I’ve tested. It feels similar to having a MagSafe battery pack on the back. I don’t mind the extra weight and thickness because it makes it easier to grip my phone case. There’s a dedicated slot at the bottom that makes sliding cards out a breeze. Just know that if you pair it with the complementary Casely case, the whole thing is bulky. But darn if it doesn’t look cute. —Brenda Stolyar.

I’m obsessed with PopSockets grips—I have one on my phone and one on my Kindle. If you’re also a fan and don’t want to get rid of the accessory with a MagSafe wallet, well, you don’t have to. The Popwallet+ is both a PopSockets grip and a wallet. It fits up to three cards (or more, depending on the thickness), and the cloth opening at the bottom makes it easy to push out the cards. The grip works the same way a standard one does, with the ability to expand and collapse. You can swap out the tops if you ever get bored with the design. —Brenda Stolyar.

Sources indicate that supcase’s MagFlip wallet and stand is extremely sturdy, and feels unbreakable. It’s constructed almost entirely out of metal, fitted with huge magnets that never let go and thick hinges around the body. You can store up to five cards in the wallet itself, and there’s an RFID-blocking card that sits at the end, though this kind of protection is largely unnecessary.

Industry observers note that it doubles as a two-height stand as well. You can kick the wallet back and prop your phone up, but if you rotate the wallet around, you can position your phone even higher with a kickstand that keeps everything stable. Even with the rugged, almost militarized construction, SupCase still offers a handful of attractive colors, including one that combines a faux leather exterior with regal gold accents. —Jacob Roach.

A lot of MagSafe wallets just feel like a pocket on the back of your phone. This one from ESR feels like an actual wallet. It comes in a variety of stylish options with a slick metal-tipped clasp and detailed construction. There’s a clear window for your ID, a roomy card pocket, and a compartment that can hold two bills. The card compartment can technically hold up to four cards, but I prefer two or three for easier access. If you want space for cash as well as the other essentials, or you want a leather-type wallet that has more design choices than some competitors, I recommend this one. —Louryn Strampe.

Sources indicate that looks like you need some MagSafe for your MagSafe. Look no further than the Valentinus wallet from Spigen. It’s constructed out of polyurethane leather and can technically hold three cards (I’m able to easily fit four). It comes with a handy card cutout at the bottom so you can quickly thumb through them. The real draw is an extra MagSafe ring built into the back of the wallet.

Industry observers note that stack a MagSafe grip on the back, mount your phone to a MagSafe car stand, or attach whatever other MagSafe accessory you want; you don’t need to take off your wallet first. You can’t charge your phone through it, but the convenience of using other accessories while keeping your wallet attached is worth the price of admission. —Jacob Roach.

Moft’s Snap-on Phone Stand and Wallet is another good kickstand wallet option. You can set it up at three angles: one for scrolling through your phone, one for streaming media, and one for video conferencing. It feels sturdy, and the case isn’t bulky. I wouldn’t put more than two cards in this one, though. I usually use it to carry my license and debit card, while the rest are in my Apple Wallet. —Brenda Stolyar.

Alternatively, Moft sells a trackable version with Apple Find My capabilities. It even comes in versions that can match your iPhone. It isn’t super roomy, but I still like it.

ESR Geo Wallet Stand for $47: Apple’s Find My app lets you track your devices if they’re lost, and ESR’s Geo wallet has it built right into the wallet itself. This is the wallet I’ve been using for the past few weeks, and outside of its Find My capabilities, I love that it strikes a great balance between size and usability. ESR says it can hold up to three cards, but I’ve been using mine with four—three cards plus my ID—and I can get them all out easily. Although having a wallet with magnetic charging pins is weird—the Find My feature requires a battery that lasts three months—you can turn it off if you don’t care for it (but then, maybe just buy a different wallet). It does kind of suck that you need a proprietary charger to recharge your wallet, though. The magnets adhere well to the back of the phone, and you can pop open the wallet and use it as a kickstand. ESR even includes a strap on the back that works as a phone grip.

In a recent development, otterBox Symmetry Series Cactus Leather MagSafe Wallet for $45: This wallet is nice and simple, thin, lightweight, has a strong hold on my phone case, and offers a dedicated fabric-covered slot at the bottom to push the cards out (I was able to fit three without much trouble). This OtterBox wallet is made from cactus-based leather, which feels nearly as luxurious as real leather. Just know that cactus leather isn’t as eco-friendly as it’s made out to be—these cases are still infused with layers of plastic.

Sources indicate that spigen MagSafe Classic LS Wallet for $40: This cool-looking wallet incorporates design inspiration from the classic Macintosh computers. The gray might seem a little bit drab, but any Apple enthusiast will likely enjoy the nod to the computers of yesteryear. It’s otherwise pretty standard fare, with space for up to three cards. I like the thumb notch, which makes it easy to slide your cards out.

Industry observers note that pelican Protector MagSafe Wallet: This MagSafe wallet is simply too bulky. It’s difficult to slip into a pocket, and we don’t think the protective hardshell is worth the trade-off since it can only hold two or three cards.

Kate Spade Latest York Morgan MagSafe Wallet: This wallet looks nice, but the finish starts to degrade with regular use. It also opened on its own once or twice, which left me worried about a card slipping out.

Ohsnap! Snap Grip Wallet: I had high hopes for this one, mainly because of its build quality. The wallet is aluminum, can hold up to eight cards (depending on whether they have raised lettering or not), has MagSafe support, and comes with a grip that doubles as a kickstand. Unfortunately, the grip is made of plastic, and it broke after a short time (it won’t fold properly back into place). The magnetic hold isn’t as strong as other MagSafe wallets, even with a MagSafe-approved case on my phone. None of that is great, especially at this high price.

Apple FineWoven MagSafe Case: Any time this wallet is separated from your iPhone, you’ll get an alert and can track it in Apple’s Find My app. It has a single slot that fits up to three cards, but to remove them, you have to take it off your iPhone and push the cards up through the slot on the back. Unfortunately, Apple’s MagSafe wallets use only the organization’s proprietary FineWoven material (made from recycled materials). It’s a commendable effort to reduce reliance on leather production, but several WIRED reviewers have stated the material doesn’t hold up well over time.

Journey Loc8 Universal MagSafe Slim Wallet: My cards would slip out of this wallet if I didn’t have it stuffed full, which makes it an obvious “Do Not Recommend” choice when so many other comparable wallets don’t have this problem.

These are the animals people most want to see photographed

📅 03 Apr 2023 | ⏱️ 3 min read (659 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNN

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that editor’s Note:  Call to Earth is a CNN editorial series committed to reporting on the environmental challenges facing our planet, together with the solutions.
  • In a recent development, originally a term used by trophy hunters in Africa, the “Massive Five” described the animals most challenging to shoot and kill: the lion, elephant, leopard, rhino, and buffalo.
  • Sources indicate that however, British photographer Graeme Green has reclaimed the narrative, creating a global “New Big Five” for wildlife photography.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that editor’s Note:  Call to Earth is a CNN editorial series committed to reporting on the environmental challenges facing our planet, together with the solutions. Rolex’s Perpetual Planet initiative has partnered with CNN to drive awareness and education around key sustainability problems and to inspire positive action.

In a recent development, originally a term used by trophy hunters in Africa, the “Massive Five” described the animals most challenging to shoot and kill: the lion, elephant, leopard, rhino, and buffalo. Nowadays, it is more loosely used to refer to some of Africa’s largest and most iconic animals.

Sources indicate that however, British photographer Graeme Green has reclaimed the narrative, creating a global “New Big Five” for wildlife photography. In 2021, 50,000 people around the world voted for the five animals they would most like to photograph, or see photographed, in the wild. Five animals were crowned the winners: the elephant, polar bear, lion, gorilla and tiger.

This week, sees the publication of “The New Substantial 5” photography book, which features images of those animals and other at-risk wildlife, from photography legends such as Ami Vitale, Steve McCurry and Paul Nicklen, and essays from famous conservationists and activists including like Jane Goodall and Paula Kahumbu.

Green notes that the book celebrates wildlife and is a global call to action on concerns impacting wildlife, including habitat loss, poaching, pollution and climate change.

Green was on assignment in Botswana at least a decade ago when he came up with the idea for a project to encourage people to “shoot with a camera, not a gun,” he notes.

“I thought this would be a way to get people really focusing on wildlife, thinking about the wildlife they love, thinking about the animals that are at risk.”.

Ten photographs that made the world wake up to climate change.

In a recent development, in total, the book includes the work of 144 globally renowned wildlife photographers from Ecuador to India. Curating the images took nearly two years of work, states Green.

According to recent reports, “I think these are some of the most beautiful and creative images that I’ve seen put together in one book,” says Green. “These are the species that we are at risk of losing.”.

According to the UN, nature is declining at an unprecedented rate, with around one million of the planet’s animal and plant species facing extinction. The “Latest Substantial 5,” all of which are threatened, act as ambassadors for what is happening in the natural world, claims Green.

In a recent development, as well as being a powerful reminder of what we stand to lose, the book also points people towards potential solutions. Featured essays explore the benefits of rewilding and the importance of indigenous communities in conservation.

A chapter on endangered species from bees to blue whales illustrates the alarming threat climate change poses to animals outside of the “New Significant 5.” “That’s only the tip of the iceberg – I could have included thousands of pictures because that’s how serious the situation is,” indicates Green.

Why a wildlife photographer took 40,000 photos to capture these extraordinary birds.

Jane Goodall, a leading conservationist who also wrote the afterword to the book, said in a press release that “we have a window of time during which we can start to heal some of the harm we have inflicted on the natural world, but only if we get together and take action now.

“I hope the photos will lead people into the wonderful worlds of these iconic species. Then, perhaps, other people will become involved in helping to create a world where wildlife can flourish for future generations to enjoy,” she said.

“The Newly introduced Significant 5: A Global Photography Project For Endangered Wildlife,” by Graeme Green, published by Earth Aware Editions, is on sale from April 4, 2023.

This story has been updated to reflect the range of problems covered by the book.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Ryan Naderi has netted some crucial goals for Derek McInnes this term.

Derek McInnes notes Rangers should not experience any anxiety about the prospect of going top of the Scottish Premiership as the Ibrox side look to extend their four-match winning run.

Rangers host in-form Falkirk on Saturday (15:00 GMT), who have won six on the bounce in the league, and victory would move McInnes' team top before leaders Celtic travel to face Hearts on Sunday.

"I don't think there should be anxiety when you're trying to go top of the league at all," McInnes said.

"Obviously, you want to be top of the league come the end of the season.

"If you've got an opportunity to go there, it's important you try and take it.".

Ryan Naderi netted an early second-half equaliser then set up Djeidi Gassama as Rangers turned a 1-0 deficit into a 3-1 lead before Aberdeen scored a consolation in Tuesday's Premiership match at Ibrox.

It was Naderi's 11th goal of the season and McInnes spoke of his awareness of the now Czech Republic international last season while managing Hearts, who have used a data analytics firm for much of their recent recruitment.

"Last January, obviously, when we first saw that Rangers were linked with Naderi, like everything else, I would say to [Hearts sporting director] Graeme Jones, 'how do they rate him?'.

In a recent development, "Because you're always curious, it's just the way it is. It's brilliant when you see other teams round about you signing a player that's not rated!

"He was someone that I think was well known to them. Brugge had an interest in Ryan, I think, and I think USG potentially had an interest in him as well but the kind of money, the fee, it just went away from them.

"The feeling was that he could help Rangers and make them better.

"I had a good conversation with Ryan when I first came in the door and what we felt this season could look like for him.

Sources indicate that "He's stood up brilliantly to the injuries to Youssef [Chermiti] and Lawrence [Shankland] and he's had to be the guy. He's led the line brilliantly and I love the goals he scores. All top strikers have intelligence to be in the right place at the right time.".

Rangers 'dug it out' despite naivety & complacency - McInnes.

Visit our Rangers page for all the latest news, analysis and fan views.

And the manager reiterated his stance about keeping hold of assets like Naderi through January.

"These conversations that I have with Jim [Gillespie, chief executive] on a regular basis about players that we should be speaking to and trying to address and secure and give them a wee bit more security and a wee bit more comfort for us, these conversations, I think, have been ongoing," McInnes remarked.

"The club's well aware of what needs to be done and what we shouldn't be doing and Ryan's been part of that conversation.".

McInnes' side won 2-1 away to Falkirk in September but the Bairns held Danny Rohl's Rangers to a 0-0 draw at Ibrox last season.

"What they have got is a bit more physicality," McInnes remarked of the Bairns.

"They can play when they want to play so they've mixed it up a bit this season, I think, and been a wee bit more pragmatic maybe at times as well, but they've still had those results that's got them where they are in the league and we've got a difficult game ahead of ourselves.".

Industry News: Pakistani astronaut becomes 1st international visitor to China's Tiangong space station (photos)

💡 Key Takeaways
  • For the first time ever, a foreign astronaut has set foot inside China's Tiangong space station.
  • It has been revealed that that pioneer is Pakistan's Muhammad Zeeshan Ali, who arrived at Tiangong aboard the Shenzhou-24 spacecraft early this morning (Nov.
  • Recent findings suggest that "The Chinese space station is always something to look forward to!" the China Manned Space Agency (CMSA) wrote in an update today (in Mandarin; translation by Google).
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

For the first time ever, a foreign astronaut has set foot inside China's Tiangong space station.

It has been revealed that that pioneer is Pakistan's Muhammad Zeeshan Ali, who arrived at Tiangong aboard the Shenzhou-24 spacecraft early this morning (Nov. 25).

Recent findings suggest that "The Chinese space station is always something to look forward to!" the China Manned Space Agency (CMSA) wrote in an update today (in Mandarin; translation by Google). "China's 'Tiangong' welcomes partners from all over the world to visit!".

In a recent development, ali, a former pilot in Pakistan's armed forces, is a payload specialist on Shenzhou-24. He found his way onto the mission thanks to a space-cooperation agreement that China signed with Pakistan in Islamabad in February 2025.

Industry observers note that ali and his two Shenzhou-24 crewmates — commander Tang Hongbo and flight engineer ​Wu Yi — enjoyed a short and smooth ride to their orbital destination. They lifted off atop a Long March 2F rocket on Tuesday (Nov. 24) at 7:18 p.m. EST (0018 GMT on Nov. 25) and reached Tiangong a little over six hours later.

It has been revealed that tang and Wu will live aboard the outpost for the usual six-month stint. Ali, however, will come home in just a week, hitching a ride with two of the three Shenzhou-23 astronauts, who arrived at Tiangong in May.

Ali will be busy during his short space stay, conducting a set of joint Chinese-Pakistani experiments.

"Four collaborative projects in biotechnology and materials are planned, with Ali also scheduled to conduct an in-orbit experiment involving photosynthetic cyanobacteria," The Times of India wrote today.

In a recent development, the third Shenzhou-23 crewmate, Zhu Yangzhu, will remain on the station until Shenzhou-24 comes home. Zhu will therefore set a Chinese record, becoming the first astronaut from his country to live in low Earth orbit for a full year.

Astronauts from the Soviet Union/Russia and the United States have already blazed this long-duration trail. The global record for longest continuous space stay is 437 days, set by cosmonaut Valeri Polyakov aboard the Mir space station from January 1994 to March 1995.

Ali is not the first person from Pakistan ever to reach space, by the way. That distinction belongs to adventurer Namira Salim, who traveled to suborbital space on a tourism flight with Virgin Galactic in October 2023.

Shenzhou-24 is the 12th crewed mission to Tiangong, a three-module, T-shaped outpost that China finished assembling in late 2022. Well, "finished" might not be the right term; China prepares to expand Tiangong, which is currently about 20% as massive as the International Space Station.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Camilo Duran's 15-goal haul this season has made him an invaluable player for a Celtic side fighting for European progression.

"Duran is priceless for us at the moment".

It would be difficult for a football manager to muster up a higher compliment for one of his players - given he should know exactly how much he did cost - but Celtic boss Martin O'Neill was rightly effusive in his praise for Camilo Duran.

With 15 goals in 23 appearances, six assists, and another late European winner on Thursday, the Colombian was once again the main man for a struggling Celtic side.

His double against Besiktas breathed life into their Europa League campaign last time out, and his late leap to nod in the winner against Torreense kept it alive.

Duran, 24, started on the bench but was brought on with just over half an hour to go as O'Neill watched his side labour against a team at the moment 13th in the Portuguese second tier.

Celtic would still be searching for their first European win were it not for their summer arrival from Qarabag, whose goals have played a key part in keeping his team within touching distance of a play-off spot with three fixtures to play.

"He's taken on this mantle of being the man and he's been fantastic," noted O'Neill, who started Duran on the bench. "We tried a similar approach against Besiktas.

Sources indicate that "Sometimes by the time Duran gets subbed on, you could be behind. But I think that's the sign of a brilliant player, he'll do something.

"He's not a major guy but he's just a super footballer, a super, super footballer.".

'He's priceless for us' - O'Neill on match winner Duran.

Duran's summer arrival was overshadowed when, just over a fortnight later, a club-record fee was paid to Bodo Glimt for another striker, Kasper Hogh.

While recent weeks have been dominated by debates over Duran or Hogh, the debate now seems settled, with the Colombian operating on a different level from his striking counterpart.

Anyone watching Celtic in Portugal would have watched Hogh find space a handful of times in the area, but repeatedly fail to find a team-mate or trouble the goalkeeper. Duran didn't need to be asked twice.

"I don't know how many touches he got, but he had the telling touch," James McFadden noted on Sportsound post-match.

Duran's goals have also proved decisive in securing domestic points against Falkirk and Hibernian, and with Celtic just a point clear of Rangers, he is indeed invaluable.

Despite his late header giving the thousands of travelling Celtic fans a thrilling end to a relatively turgid game, the intervention is another significant moment in a season that is threatening to unravel if individual performances fail to continue papering over glaring deficiencies across the park.

If the lively Jota - who lasted 74 minutes - was not creating chances, tormenting full-backs or digging out enticing crosses in the first half, Celtic seemed without any real blueprint of attack.

Yang and Luke McCowan's involvements were limited at best, Hogh's chance to stake a claim was sub-par to be kind, and there was no driving force from the middle of the park to show some impetus.

Recent findings suggest that arithmetically, Celtic can still finish in any position in the Europa League table. But if they are to claim a playoff or automatic qualification spot, they will need Duran to remain in such a rich vein of form.

Target on Wednesday reported its best sales growth in more than five years and beat Wall Street's revenue expectations, the latest signs of its turnaround strategy taking hold.

Sources indicate that the retailer mentioned its net sales grew 7.1% during the fiscal third quarter. Comparable sales rose 5.6%, compared with StreetAccount estimates of up 3.8%. That growth was boosted by a 5% increase in comparable traffic, Target added.

"[It's] a healthy sign that guests are responding to our changes and choosing Target more often," CEO Michael Fiddelke told reporters.

Digital comparable sales jumped nearly 10% during the quarter.

Encouraged by the growth, Target raised its full-year guidance, upping its net sales growth guidance by 1 percentage point to around 6%. It's also expecting full-year operating income margin rate to be around 6.2%, which includes roughly 1.1 percentage points of benefit from tariff refunds.

The company also said it's now projecting full-year earnings per share to be in a range of $10.65 to $11.40, compared with prior guidance of between $9.90 and $10.90.

According to recent reports, "The changes we've made across our assortment and guest experience are adding up," Fiddelke told reporters. "While we're encouraged by the progress, we know there's more work ahead to sustain this momentum and deliver consistent growth over time.".

Target shares climbed about 7% in afternoon trading Wednesday.

Here's how the company performed in its fiscal third quarter compared with what Wall Street was expecting, based on a survey of analysts by LSEG:.

For the quarter ended Oct. 31, Target reported net income of $1.21 billion, or $2.65 per share, up from $689 million, or $1.51 per share, a year earlier.

According to recent reports, this year, the company mentioned it's invested approximately $3.8 billion in capital expenditures, up nearly $1 billion from last year. Because of those returns, Fiddelke said Target is now expecting to invest between $5 billion and $6 billion in capex next year.

On a call with analysts, he added that those investments will go toward more store remodels, technology, supply chain improvements, among other initiatives.

The firm noted it saw particular strength in beauty, which saw 9% growth, and food and beverage, where sales increased nearly 7%. The retailer added that net sales rose in all three months of the third quarter, with the strongest performance during the back-to-school season.

Fiddelke told reporters the quarter's strength showed "continued progress" toward Target's priorities that it outlined at the beginning of its turnaround.

In a recent development, as it looks to the holiday season, Target said it's marketing thousands of products priced at $5 and under, along with fresh artificial intelligence-powered shopping experiences to drive engagement. Fiddelke said Target is "encouraged" by shopping behaviors it's seen so far in the current quarter.

The significant-box retailer has been showing signs of returning to growth, as it sees stronger sales trends after years of flat revenue. The results come after Target last quarter hiked its full fiscal-year outlook and said it saw "broad-based" strength across its various categories.

It's also lowered prices on more than 10,000 items in an effort to get customers back into its stores, especially as consumer sentiment lags and inflation remains high. The retailer said on Wednesday that it cut prices on an additional roughly 2,000 items during the third quarter.

Target's stock is up more than 70% this year.

NASA smashed into an asteroid. Now Hera has revealed a strange upcoming world

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (809 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The European Space Agency's (ESA) Hera spacecraft has captured its first close-up image of the Didymos asteroid system, offering scientists a surprising latest perspective on the site of NASA's historic asteroid deflection experiment.
  • According to recent reports, on September 26, 2022, NASA's DART spacecraft deliberately crashed into Dimorphos, the smaller of the two asteroids in the system.
  • Recent findings suggest that the image was taken from a distance of 60 km using Hera's monochromatic Asteroid Framing Camera, which captures images in black and white.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The European Space Agency's (ESA) Hera spacecraft has captured its first close-up image of the Didymos asteroid system, offering scientists a surprising latest perspective on the site of NASA's historic asteroid deflection experiment.

According to recent reports, on September 26, 2022, NASA's DART spacecraft deliberately crashed into Dimorphos, the smaller of the two asteroids in the system. Hera's latest image provides a look at its larger companion, Didymos, from a side that scientists had not previously seen in such detail.

Recent findings suggest that the image was taken from a distance of 60 km using Hera's monochromatic Asteroid Framing Camera, which captures images in black and white. Although most of Dimorphos, which measures 151 m across, is concealed in shadow, the much larger Didymos, with a diameter of 780 m, is clearly visible.

A Surprisingly Different Side of Asteroid Didymos.

Recent findings suggest that "The first thing we noted was wow!" observes Hera Principal Investigator Patrick Michel, Director of Research at CNRS / Observatoire de la Côte d'Azur. "This is the other side of Didymos from the one that DART's camera revealed us shortly before impact, so this feels like looking at a whole upcoming world.

"This side of Didymos has the same central ridge along its equator that we saw before, but otherwise appears very different, with multiple boulders and craters and what look like patterns of grooves or ridges.".

The newly revealed terrain raises intriguing questions about how the asteroid's surface developed and whether NASA's collision with Dimorphos may have left traces on its larger neighbor.

When DART struck Dimorphos, the impact sent material flying into space. Scientists believe some of that debris may have traveled across the roughly 1 km separating the two asteroids and reached Didymos. Determining whether this material contributed to the features now visible on its surface will be an important part of Hera's investigation.

ESA's Hera mission scientist Michael Kueppers adds: "Since we expect a lot of impact-ejected material to have made it across the approximately 1 km of space from Dimorphos to Didymos, it may be that some of these characteristics originate from this transport of material, and we have exciting work ahead of us to sort it out. We look forward to seeing much more of both bodies and systemically mapping all the changes we identify.".

NASA's DART Mission Changed an Asteroid's Orbit.

Although Dimorphos is largely obscured in Hera's new image, it holds a remarkable place in space exploration history. It became the first object in the Solar System to have its orbit measurably altered by human activity.

In a recent development, NASA achieved this milestone by sending the 580 kg DART spacecraft into Dimorphos at approximately 6.1 km/s. The collision reduced the time the smaller asteroid takes to complete an orbit around Didymos by about 33 minutes, give or take a minute. That change was substantially greater than scientists had anticipated.

Sources indicate that the experiment demonstrated that striking an asteroid with a spacecraft can change its motion through space. This approach, known as kinetic impact deflection, could potentially be used to redirect a dangerous asteroid before it reaches Earth.

Hera Begins Its Investigation of NASA's Asteroid Impact.

After a two-year journey, Hera has reached the double asteroid system, located 196.8 million km from Earth. The spacecraft is now preparing for a detailed 'crash site investigation' to examine the consequences of NASA's groundbreaking experiment.

Recent findings suggest that while DART demonstrated that an asteroid's orbit could be changed through a deliberate collision, Hera will help scientists understand the physical processes behind the result. By examining both asteroids and documenting their characteristics, researchers hope to improve their ability to predict how future asteroid deflection attempts might work.

In a recent development, the findings could help transform kinetic impact deflection from a successful one-time demonstration into a dependable, repeatable planetary defense technique. Such a capability could prove critical if an asteroid were ever discovered on a collision course with Earth.

Recent findings suggest that "Seeing this image is a hugely exciting moment for the whole Hera family," comments Hera mission manager Ian Carnelli. "It has taken years of hard work and dedication to reach this point - but we're motivated to know that the adventure is only beginning!".

The mission's next major reveal is scheduled for November 25, when detailed images of both Didymos and Dimorphos will be unveiled, giving scientists and the public a closer look at the asteroids involved in humanity's first successful asteroid deflection experiment.
